truths.summary: Never call player:getCharacterTraits():get(handle) or :add(handle) or :remove(handle) on a CharacterTrait that was NOT registered via TraitFactory.addTrait. All three NPE at CharacterTraits.java:67 due to unboxing null Boolean from Map.get.
truths.details: The CharacterTraits Java class stores trait state as Map<CharacterTrait, Boolean>. Line 67 does map.get(trait).booleanValue() — auto-unbox NPEs on null. The set() and add() methods call get() internally to detect state change for events, so they crash too. Vanilla traits never hit this because TraitFactory populates the map with all registered traits as Boolean.FALSE entries at character init. Custom traits registered ONLY through CharacterTrait.register() are absent from the map. Symptom: NPE on any trait op including add(). Fix: register via TraitFactory.addTrait at OnGameBoot. Never write the 'safe presence check' guard `if not traits:get(handle)` for a custom trait — the guard itself NPEs.
evidence: Decompiled stack: CharacterTraits.add(line 82) -> CharacterTraits.set(line 71) -> CharacterTraits.get(line 67) -> Boolean.booleanValue on null
Two prior MasterySystem fix attempts both wrote `if not traits:get(handle)` as the safe pattern — both fixes themselves NPE'd in production

truths.details:
B42 API replaces the per-stat getter / setter methods on IsoGameCharacter stats (getStress, getPanic, getEndurance, etc.) with a generic enum-keyed API on Stats.

## Stats class API (vanilla_source-confirmed)

Source: javap zombie.characters.CharacterStat.class (B42.18.0, extract 2026-05-13). All entries are `public static final zombie.characters.CharacterStat`:

  NICOTINE_WITHDRAWAL, PAIN, PANIC, POISON, SANITY, SICKNESS,

  ZOMBIE_FEVER, ZOMBIE_INFECTION

## Runtime probe cross-check (2026-05-31)
- 12 PRESENT in runtime probe (BV2): BOREDOM, ENDURANCE, FATIGUE, FITNESS, HUNGER, PAIN, PANIC, STRESS, THIRST, UNHAPPINESS, ZOMBIE_FEVER, ZOMBIE_INFECTION - all in source enum.
- 3 ABSENT in runtime probe: STRENGTH, HEALTH, DRUNKENNESS - ALSO absent from source enum (the runtime negatives were correct).
- 12 not probed at runtime (ANGER, DISCOMFORT, FOOD_SICKNESS, IDLENESS, INTOXICATION, MORALE, NICOTINE_WITHDRAWAL, POISON, SANITY, SICKNESS, TEMPERATURE, WETNESS) - confirmed PRESENT by source pin alone. (Previously listed as UNVERIFIED; promoted to PRESENT 2026-05-31 per vanilla_source.)

## Safe read pattern
```lua
local function safeStatGet(stats, statEnum, default)
    default = default or 0
    if not stats or not stats.get or not statEnum then return default end
    local val = stats:get(statEnum)
    return val ~= nil and val or default
end
```

Calling stats:get(CharacterStat.STRENGTH/HEALTH/DRUNKENNESS) with the nil enum value crashes (`attempted index: get of non-table: nil` or downstream NPE). Always guard `if statEnum then ...`.

truths.summary: CharacterTrait.register(id) CREATES a new trait — throws in B42.18 when called on already-registered ids. To LOOK UP an existing vanilla trait by string id use CharacterTrait.get(ResourceLocation.of(id)).
truths.details: Two distinct API surfaces share confusingly similar names: (1) CharacterTrait.register('ns:id') creates/registers a NEW CharacterTrait in the CharacterTraitDefinition registry. In B42.18 it throws (NPE or RuntimeException) when called on an id that already exists — which is every vanilla trait. (2) CharacterTrait.get(ResourceLocation.of('ns:id')) is a pure lookup of an already-registered trait, safe to call repeatedly, returns nil if not found. Use register() ONLY for traits your mod is introducing. Use get(ResourceLocation.of(...)) for vanilla trait lookups (e.g. 'base:packmule', 'base:brave'). MTD/More Traits Dynamic uses get() exclusively and works reliably. MasterySystem 2026-05-28 originally used register() for both paths; switched to get(ResourceLocation.of(...)) for vanilla after in-game testing showed register() crashes on every vanilla trait reward grant.

truths.summary: CharacterTrait.get(ResourceLocation) returns nil for custom/runtime-registered traits. Use CharacterTrait.register(id) for both custom AND vanilla traits — it returns the existing handle for pre-registered traits. Also: player:hasTrait() NPEs on custom traits; use traits:get(handle) instead.
truths.details:
There are TWO different CharacterTrait APIs in B42 and they are NOT interchangeable for custom traits:

**CharacterTrait.get(ResourceLocation.of("namespace:key"))** — only works for traits already in the Java CharacterTraitDefinition static registry before the game loaded. Returns nil for traits registered at runtime via `CharacterTrait.register()`. This is suitable for vanilla traits ('base:lucky', etc.).

**CharacterTrait.register("Namespace:id")** — registers a trait AND returns a handle. For already-registered traits (vanilla), register() returns the existing handle rather than creating a duplicate. Safe for BOTH vanilla and custom traits. Required for traits your mod registers at runtime.

**player:hasTrait(handle)** — internally calls CharacterTraits.get() (the static map) which returns null for runtime-registered traits → causes NPE unboxing the Boolean result. Never call this for custom traits.

**Correct pattern for custom traits:**
```lua
local _traitCache = {}
local function resolveTrait(id)
    if _traitCache[id] ~= nil then return _traitCache[id] or nil end
    if not CharacterTrait or type(CharacterTrait.register) ~= 'function' then
        _traitCache[id] = false; return nil
    end
    local handle = CharacterTrait.register('MyMod:' .. id)
    _traitCache[id] = handle or false
    return handle or nil
end

local function hasTrait(player, handle)
    if not handle then return false end
    local traits = player:getCharacterTraits()
    return traits and traits:get(handle) and true or false
end

local function addTrait(player, handle)
    if not handle then return end
    local traits = player:getCharacterTraits()
    if not traits then return end
    if not traits:get(handle) then traits:add(handle) end
end

local function removeTrait(player, handle)
    if not handle then return end
    local traits = player:getCharacterTraits()
    if not traits then return end
    if traits:get(handle) then traits:remove(handle) end
end
```

Note: `not traits:get(handle)` is the safe presence check — handles both nil (not in map) and false (in map but inactive) cases uniformly. Do NOT use `hasTrait ~= nil and not hasTrait` as this skips the nil case.

For vanilla traits, CharacterTrait.register('base:lucky') also works (returns the existing handle safely).

truths.summary: Custom CharacterTraits added at runtime via getCharacterTraits():add() MUST be registered through TraitFactory.addTrait() at OnGameBoot. CharacterTrait.register() alone is NOT enough and will cause NPE on every player trait operation.
truths.details: B42.18 Java behaviour: player:getCharacterTraits() returns a Map<CharacterTrait, Boolean>. That map is seeded ONLY with TraitFactory-registered traits at character init. Calling map.get(handle) on an unregistered trait returns null, and CharacterTraits.java:67 unboxes it via Boolean.booleanValue() -> NullPointerException. The chain CharacterTraits.add(handle) -> set() -> get() means even add() crashes for unregistered traits. CharacterTrait.register('ns:id') creates a handle in the CharacterTraitDefinition registry (sufficient for filter UI and ResourceLocation resolution) but does NOT register with TraitFactory and does NOT seed the player map. The ONLY safe pattern for runtime-added custom traits is: (1) call TraitFactory.addTrait(id, name, cost, desc, isProfession, isFree) at Events.OnGameBoot for every flag trait you intend to ever add; (2) use player:hasTrait(handle) for presence (iterates trait ArrayList, not the buggy map.get); (3) then player:getCharacterTraits():add(handle) and :remove(handle) work without NPE. Vanilla traits work directly because all vanilla traits are TraitFactory-registered and pre-seeded. MasterySystem hit this bug repeatedly until the 2026-05-28 refactor moved registration to OnGameBoot via TraitFactory.addTrait.
evidence: In-game B42.18 NPE log 2026-05-28: java.lang.NullPointerException at zombie.characters.traits.CharacterTraits.get(CharacterTraits.java:67) for every applySkillTraits/clearSkillTraits call

truths.summary: To dynamically lower/raise a perk level in B42 use player:LoseLevel(perk)/player:LevelPerk(perk) paired with player:getXp():setXPToLevel(perk, level) to preserve XP correctly.
truths.details:
When a trait gain/loss should change a player's perk level (e.g. gaining 'Dextrous' boosts a skill), use this pattern:

**Lower level by 1:**
```lua
local savedXP = player:getXp():getXP(perk) -- save XP within current level
player:LoseLevel(perk)
player:getXp():setXPToLevel(perk, player:getPerkLevel(perk))
player:getXp():AddXP(perk, savedXP)
```

**Raise level by 1:**
```lua
local savedXP = player:getXp():getXP(perk)
player:LevelPerk(perk)
player:getXp():setXPToLevel(perk, player:getPerkLevel(perk))
player:getXp():AddXP(perk, savedXP)
```

Always save and restore XP within the current level so the XP bar doesn't reset to zero after the level change. `setXPToLevel` sets total accumulated XP to the threshold for that level; `AddXP` tops up the saved intra-level progress.

XP boost (multiplier) is separate: `player:getXp():getPerkBoost(perk)` / `setPerkBoost(perk, value)`. Max boost value is 3.
evidence: <local-path> — DTEMaddTrait/DTEMremoveTrait perk adjustment block

DTEMutils.lua DTEMremoveTrait — calls player:LoseLevel(perk) for trait-remove level reverts
Paired with player:getXp():AddXP(perk, ±n) to keep XP coherent with the level change

truths.summary: Wrap Events[name].Add at shared-file load to passively intercept every callback every mod registers — enables cross-mod instrumentation (timing, logging, error trapping) without modifying any other mod.
truths.details: B42 Events table is a Lua-side dispatcher where each event has an .Add method that stores callbacks. Replacing Events[name].Add at file load means every subsequent registration (from any mod, including vanilla) flows through your shim. Pattern: save origAdd, replace .Add with a function that takes (self, fn), builds a wrapped fn that the original .Add then stores. The wrap must guard on a runtime flag (e.g. MLog.watch.events) so the cost is one boolean check per fire when disabled. Do NOT use pcall around the wrapped callback (broken in B42.15+); let errors propagate so the engine's normal handling runs. For error capture, override print() separately and scan for engine-error patterns. Pattern lives in shared/ — no Events.X.Add(bootstrap) is needed because we mutate the .Add method directly at file load, not via subscription. Curate the watched-event list to balance coverage vs noise; OnTick / OnPlayerUpdate should log at TRACE only. MLog v1.1 implements this in shared/MLog_EventsWatcher.lua.

MLog v1.1 shared/MLog_ErrorCapture.lua complements with print() override scanning for ERROR_PATTERNS (NPE, RuntimeException, attempted index, ...) and re-entrancy guard to avoid recursion via MLog.error -> writeLine -> print
Vanilla Events table is Lua-backed so Events[name].Add is a plain function field replaceable at load time
Wrap is per-event from a curated allowlist (lifecycle / periodic / actions / cross-process / context-menu / per-frame) tiered by log level so trace-only events stay invisible at default debug level

truths.summary: Wrap ISInventoryItem.renderItemIcon to draw overlays (condition bars, status icons) directly on inventory item cells using pane:drawRect()
truths.details:
Hook pattern for inventory item cell overlays:
```lua
local orig = ISInventoryItem.renderItemIcon
ISInventoryItem.renderItemIcon = function(self, x, y, w, h)
    orig(self, x, y, w, h)
    local item = self.item
    if not item then return end
    -- Draw overlay bar at bottom of icon cell
    local pct = tonumber(item:getCondition()) / math.max(1, tonumber(item:getMaxCondition()))
```

truths.summary: Pass a pseudo-perk value (e.g. 'characterInitialization') to LevelPerk handlers on game start to run a full trait-check pass without duplicating condition logic.
truths.details:
Dynamic trait systems often hook `Events.LevelPerk` to react when a perk increases. To also run the full trait evaluation at game start (so restored saves have correct traits), call the same evaluation function from `Events.OnGameStart` / `Events.EveryOneMinute` / `Events.OnCharacterLoaded`, passing a sentinel string as the `perk` argument:

```lua
local function evaluateTraits(player, perk)
    if not player or player:isDead() then return end
    -- perk == "characterInitialization" means: check everything
    if vars.StrengthTraitDynamic or perk == "characterInitialization" then
        if perk == Perks.Strength or perk == "characterInitialization" then
            -- check strength-gated traits
        end
    end
end

Events.LevelPerk.Add(evaluateTraits)
Events.OnGameStart.Add(function()
    local p = getSpecificPlayer(0)
    if p then evaluateTraits(p, "characterInitialization") end
end)
```

This avoids duplicating all condition branches and ensures save-reload consistency. Use a string constant like `"characterInitialization"` that can never collide with a real `Perks.*` enum value.

truths.summary: B42 MP serializes timed actions by introspecting Class:new's compiled parameter names; never override :new on net-synced shared timed actions — use getDuration/complete/method overrides instead.
truths.details: Mechanism (disassembled from B42.19 zombie/core/NetTimedAction.class): (1) CLIENT, NetTimedAction.set(IsoPlayer, KahluaTable) lines 44-51: takes action.getMetatable().rawget("new") as a LuaClosure, reads Prototype.numParams and Prototype.locvars (the DECLARED parameter names of the CURRENT new at queue time), and for each param name i=1..numParams-1 stores action[paramName] into actionArgs (PZNetKahluaTableImpl/LinkedHashMap, insertion order preserved; nil becomes PZNetKahluaNull). (2) write() line 188-192 sends type, name, actionArgs. (3) SERVER, parse() lines 151-175: resolves the class table via LuaManager.get(type) and the constructor via LuaManager.getFunctionObject(type..".new") — the SERVER'S OWN global new, by name, at parse time — then LuaCaller.protectedCall(newFn, classTable, actionArgs values in order). Consequences: (a) a Lua :new override whose parameter names differ from the instance-field names vanilla new sets (e.g. BB Medical's new(doctor,...) vs vanilla new(character,...) which sets o.character) makes the client capture nil -> server constructs with null character -> crash like 'ISApplyBandage.lua:177 attempted index: getPerkLevel of non-table: null'; (b) a vararg wrapper new(...) captures ZERO args (numParams=1); (c) a client-only :new override diverges from the server which runs vanilla new. truths.summary: Inject custom items into existing loot tables at runtime by patching ProceduralDistributions.list with duplicate-check guard
truths.details:
Pattern for adding items to existing distribution tables without overwriting:
```lua
local dist = ProceduralDistributions.list
if dist and dist['ZombieInventory'] then
    local items = dist['ZombieInventory'].items
    -- Check for duplicate first
    local found = false
    for i = 1, #items, 2 do
        if items[i] == 'Base.MyItem' then found = true; break end
    end
    if not found then
        table.insert(items, 'Base.MyItem')
        table.insert(items, 0.5)  -- weight
    end
end
```
Items and weights are interleaved: `{itemName, weight, itemName, weight, ...}`. Always check for duplicates to prevent double-insertion on module reload. Run in server-only code (after `if isClient() then return end`). No ModData needed — this is in-memory only and resets on restart.

truths.summary: After adding or removing a trait on a client, call sendClientCommand + sendPlayerStatsChange(player) to sync the change to the server and back to all clients.
truths.details:
Trait mutations made on the client (via `player:getCharacterTraits():add/remove()`) are local-only until explicitly synced. After any trait add/remove:

1. `sendClientCommand("ModuleID", "addTrait"|"removeTrait", { trait = traitIdString })` — notifies the server
2. `sendPlayerStatsChange(player)` — broadcasts the stats/trait update to all clients

Wrap `sendPlayerStatsChange` in `pcall` since it may not be available in all contexts:
```lua
if isClient and isClient() and sendPlayerStatsChange and player then
    pcall(function() sendPlayerStatsChange(player) end)
end
```

truths.summary: B42 trait resolution uses CharacterTrait.get(ResourceLocation.of(namespace:key)) with a local cache table — never pass raw strings to hasTrait/addTrait/removeTrait.
truths.details:
In B42, traits are Java objects resolved via `CharacterTrait.get(ResourceLocation.of("namespace:key"))`. The namespace is `"base"` for vanilla traits and the mod ID for custom ones (e.g. `"DynamicTraits:id"`). Always cache the resolved object in a local table keyed by the input string to avoid repeated Java lookups. Cache failed lookups as `false` (not `nil`) so the cache sentinel works with `if resolvedTraits[key] ~= nil` checks. Example pattern:

```lua
local resolvedTraits = {}
local function resolveTrait(id)
    if resolvedTraits[id] ~= nil then return resolvedTraits[id] or nil end
    if not CharacterTrait or not ResourceLocation then
        resolvedTraits[id] = false; return nil
    end
    local t = CharacterTrait.get(ResourceLocation.of("base:" .. string.lower(id)))
    resolvedTraits[id] = t or false
    return t
end
```

For trait IDs that may be in a custom mod namespace, try the mod namespace first, then fall back to `base:`.

truths.summary: player:hasTrait(), traits:add(), and traits:remove() ALL NPE when the trait key is absent from the character's Java Map — none are safe to call speculatively. Guard in Lua only.
truths.details:
All three CharacterTraits Java methods share the same root bug: they call CharacterTraits.get(key) which does Map.get(key).booleanValue(). If the key is absent (trait was never registered on this character instance), Map.get() returns null and booleanValue() throws NullPointerException.

This means:
- traits:remove(handle) NPEs if trait not added — as previously known
- player:hasTrait(handle) ALSO NPEs for the same reason — it cannot be used as a guard
- traits:add(handle) may also be unsafe if the underlying map has not been initialised for this handle

The ONLY safe guard is Lua-side tracking: record which traits have been applied in ModData or a Lua table, and only call Java CharacterTraits methods for handles you KNOW are already in the character's map. Do not call hasTrait(), add(), or remove() speculatively on a trait that may never have been touched for this player.

truths.summary: Custom CharacterTrait registry IDs (namespace:traitid) must be fully lowercase. Registry keys are case-sensitive; mixed-case IDs resolve to null and cause a CharacterTraitDefinition.<init> NPE at line 38 during load.
truths.details:
When registering a custom trait via CharacterTrait.register(id), the id string (both the namespace block and the trait value) must be entirely lowercase. B42's registry uses case-sensitive key lookup; vanilla trait IDs (e.g. 'base:brave', 'base:athletic') are all lowercase.

Passing a mixed-case id such as 'base:MyTrait' or 'mods:UpperCaseTrait' causes the registry lookup to return null. The null is then passed into CharacterTraitDefinition.<init>, which NPEs at line 38 during the definition construction — typically manifesting as a crash at mod load time with no helpful Lua-layer message.

Fix: always construct trait IDs as fully lowercase strings:
```lua
local id = "mynamespace:mytraitid"  -- all lowercase
CharacterTrait.register(id)
```

Basis: MED1 (BB_CommonSense_Medical) B42.19 runtime log showing CharacterTraitDefinition.<init> NPE traced back to a mixed-case ID.
evidence: MED1 (BB_CommonSense_Medical) B42.19 runtime log: CharacterTraitDefinition.<init> NPE at line 38 — root cause traced to mixed-case trait registration ID
Vanilla character_traits.txt (B42.19): all 100+ vanilla trait IDs use lowercase namespace + lowercase key (e.g. 'base:brave', 'base:lightfooted')
CharacterTrait.register() B42.19 decompiled: calls registry.get(id) with case-sensitive key — no case-normalisation applied before lookup

truths.summary: On IsoCell, BOTH getObjectList() and getObjectListForLua() exist in B42.18 - with DIFFERENT return types. getObjectListForLua() returns java.util.List (ArrayList, iterable via :size()/:get(i)). getObjectList() returns java.util.Set (NOT iterable as a list on the Kahlua bridge - shows up as opaque userdata). Use getObjectListForLua() for Lua iteration; getObjectList() is for Java-side consumers.
truths.details:
REVISED 2026-05-31 in-place: the prior 'replaced in B42.17+' wording was wrong - both methods coexist on IsoCell with different return types. Vanilla source pin VS-2026-05-31-bucketA-getobjectlistforlua-method-scope.json via javap shows:
```
public java.util.Set<zombie.iso.IsoMovingObject>  getObjectList();
public java.util.List<zombie.iso.IsoMovingObject> getObjectListForLua();
```

## Lua-side behaviour
- `cell:getObjectListForLua()` returns a Java ArrayList. Iterate with :size() + :get(i). Safe.
- `cell:getObjectList()` returns a Set. On the Kahlua bridge it surfaces as userdata WITHOUT :size()/:get(i) (T25 runtime confirmed: `cell.getObjectList.call=non-java-list|type=userdata`). Treating it as iterable will crash.
- Neither method is a top-level Lua global (T25 confirmed: `global.getObjectListForLua=absent`, `global.getObjectList=absent`).

## Author guidance
Use `cell:getObjectListForLua()`. Avoid `cell:getObjectList()` from Lua entirely.

## Zombie list quirk
Per CLAUDE.md: `cell:getZombieList()` is removed in B42 - use `cell:getObjectListForLua()` and filter with `instanceof(obj, 'IsoZombie')`.

truths.summary: ISChat present-at-load is env-dependent: nil at OnGameStart on SP context (per original observation), but a table on c2d client at OnGameStart (T39/C2D 2026-05-31 observation). The recommended pattern — hook ISChat from `Events.OnChatWindowInit.Add` instead of `Events.OnGameStart.Add` — remains correct regardless: OnChatWindowInit ALWAYS fires after ISChat is initialized, so it's the safe attachment point in any environment.
truths.details:
Hooking ISChat.onCommandEntered or other ISChat methods inside Events.OnGameStart.Add can crash with 'attempt to index a nil value (global ISChat)' because the ISChat panel may not yet exist at that point.

The safe event is OnChatWindowInit:
```lua
Events.OnChatWindowInit.Add(function()
    local originalFn = ISChat.onCommandEntered
    ISChat.onCommandEntered = function(self)
        -- custom logic
        originalFn(self)
    end
end)
```

OnChatWindowInit fires after the chat panel is fully constructed and ISChat is guaranteed non-nil.

## Env-dependent ISChat-at-OnGameStart state (2026-06-01 clarification)

Observed values for `type(ISChat)` at OnGameStart fire:

| Environment | ISChat type at OnGameStart |
|---|---|
| SP client (original observation) | `nil` |
| c2d client (C2D session 2026-05-31) | `table` (present) |
| hosted-host player | not yet probed |

C2D evidence: `PZTEMP-MP-CL|target.ischat-hook|ISChat.type.at-OnGameStart|table`

The original truth wording implied ISChat is nil at OnGameStart universally. The c2d observation refutes that universal scope, but the recommendation (use `OnChatWindowInit` for safety) is still correct because (a) it covers ALL environments, (b) it's the only event guaranteed to fire AFTER ISChat is fully initialised in every context. Treat the recommendation as env-portable; the 'why' is env-dependent.

truths.summary: To extend ISEquipWeaponAction behavior, wrap perform() not complete() — complete() wrapping causes infinite loops due to vanilla reciprocal handgun-slot logic.
truths.details:
See also truth b42.weapon.equipaction-complete-wrap-loop for the failure mode.

The safe extension points for ISEquipWeaponAction:
1. Wrap perform() with an early-exit guard for already-equipped weapons
2. Use Events.OnPlayerAttackFinished for post-attack off-hand restoration
3. Never wrap complete() — vanilla handgun logic in complete() reciprocally triggers equip events

```lua
local origPerform = ISEquipWeaponAction.perform
ISEquipWeaponAction.perform = function(self)
    -- early exit: prevent loop when primary already set
    if self.character:getPrimaryHandItem() then
        -- do not origPerform if already equipped
        return
    end
    origPerform(self)
end
```

truths.summary: Test whether an item is 'any hat' generically via item:getBodyLocation() == ItemBodyLocation.HAT or == ItemBodyLocation.FULL_HAT. Vanilla hats share no common functional Tag, so tags[] recipe matching cannot express 'any headwear' -- BodyLocation is the correct axis.
truths.details: Needed a way for a craftRecipe/Lua check to accept 'any vanilla hat, helmet, hard hat, pot, or colander' (anything occupying the single head equip slot) without enumerating 100+ item ids. Checked every Hat_* item in the installed 42.20.3 media/scripts/generated/items/clothing.txt: they only carry cosmetic tags like `base:isfirefuel;base:isfiretinder`, never a shared 'hat' or 'headwear' tag, so a tags[] recipe input line cannot generically match them. All of them do share `BodyLocation = base:hat` (a minority use `base:fullhat`), which is readable in Lua as item:getBodyLocation() and compared against the global ItemBodyLocation table's HAT / FULL_HAT constants. Confirmed ItemBodyLocation.HAT and ItemBodyLocation.FULL_HAT are real, currently-used globals (not a guess) via vanilla's own ISWearClothing.lua, which keys a lookup table by them directly: `WearClothingAnimations[ItemBodyLocation.HAT] = "Face"` and `WearClothingAnimations[ItemBodyLocation.FULL_HAT] = "Face"` (both grouped into the same animation region, confirming they're the correct pairing for 'the hat slot' as one concept). Scanning the full clothing.txt also surfaced every other BodyLocation this game uses (belt, mask, maskeyes, maskfull, jackethat, sweaterhat, fullsuithead, etc.) -- mask/maskeyes/maskfull are separate, simultaneously-wearable slots (e.g. a gas mask over a cap), not part of 'the hat slot'.

truths.summary: SandboxVars are not reliably populated at require/file-load time — read them in Events.OnInitWorld, not at module level.
truths.details:
SandboxVars (and sandbox page sub-tables like SandboxVars.MyMod) are not guaranteed to exist when Lua files are first required. Apply any sandbox-driven config inside an Events.OnInitWorld.Add(fn) callback:

```lua
-- WRONG: may be nil at require time
local myFlag = SandboxVars.MyMod and SandboxVars.MyMod.EnableFeature

-- CORRECT:
local myFlag = false
Events.OnInitWorld.Add(function()
    local sv = SandboxVars and SandboxVars.MyMod
    if sv then
        myFlag = (sv.EnableFeature == true or sv.EnableFeature == 1)
    end
end)
```

OnInitWorld fires after the world is initialized and SandboxVars is fully populated for both SP and MP.
evidence: 3666281346 VM_MultipliersApply.lua — install() registers Events.OnInitWorld.Add(applyNow) rather than calling at require time

truths.summary: Calling next() or pairs() on the SandboxVars Java proxy throws in B42. Access sandbox options by exact declared key only (SandboxVars.MyOption); never iterate the proxy as a Lua table.
truths.details: SandboxVars is a Java-backed proxy object, not a plain Lua table. The Kahlua __index metamethod forwards known-key lookups to the underlying Java SandboxOptions object, but the proxy does not implement __pairs or a compatible next() traversal. Attempting `for k,v in pairs(SandboxVars) do` or `next(SandboxVars)` throws a RuntimeException or returns unexpected results. Safe pattern: always access SandboxVars by the exact declared option key. Confidence is medium — direct runtime probe on B42.18+ not yet performed; treat as probable until test-server confirms.
evidence: Noted as common B42 trap in Brain/SKILL.md: 'SandboxVars are first-init defaults only. Runtime admin config belongs in ModData.' Java proxy table behaviour observed during MasterySystem audit 2026-06-04.
Basis: Kahlua proxy __index only; no __pairs/__next implementation documented in B42 source inspection to date.

truths.summary: setWornItem/getWornItem take a ResourceLocation object, not a string; item:getBodyLocation() returns a ResourceLocation directly — pass it through without tostring().
truths.details:
player:setWornItem(loc, item) and player:getWornItem(loc) expect loc to be a ResourceLocation object, not a plain string. Use item:getBodyLocation() to obtain the correct ResourceLocation and pass it directly:

```lua
local loc = item:getBodyLocation()  -- ResourceLocation, not string
player:setWornItem(loc, item)
local worn = player:getWornItem(loc)
```

truths.summary: traits:contains(t) is the safe replacement for player:hasTrait(t) on custom traits — ArrayList.contains() never touches CharacterTraits static map
truths.details:
player:hasTrait(CharacterTrait) routes through CharacterTraits.get(key) — a static Java Map lookup. For any trait not in that map (all runtime-registered custom traits), Map.get() returns null and .booleanValue() throws NullPointerException.

The fix is NOT Lua-side bookkeeping — it is using the player's instance ArrayList directly:

```lua
local traits = player:getCharacterTraits()  -- Java ArrayList<CharacterTrait>
-- safe check:
if traits:contains(t) then traits:remove(t) end
if not traits:contains(t) then traits:add(t) end
```

ArrayList.contains() iterates the list by object equality — it does not call CharacterTraits.get() and cannot NPE. This is the minimal one-line replacement for every hasTrait() call that guards an add/remove of a custom trait.

Addendum to truth b42.api.character_traits_remove_npe_guard: that truth's 'Lua-side tracking only' conclusion is overstated — traits:contains(t) is a safe Java-side check.
evidence: MasteryManager.lua clearSkillTraits and applySkillTraits crashed x10 with NPE at CharacterTraits.get:67 / IsoGameCharacter.hasTrait:5565 even when hasTrait was used as a guard before remove()
Replacing player:hasTrait(t) with traits:contains(t) in all four call sites (lines 114, 118, 140, 147, 153 of MasteryManager.lua) eliminated all crashes — confirmed B42.18 singleplayer

truths.summary: IsoGameCharacter:getAttachedItems():getItem(locationName) throws a Java RuntimeException 'no such location' if the locationName is not registered on that character's AttachedItems group. Iterate the group first via getGroup():getLocationByIndex(i):getId() and only call getItem() for confirmed-registered names.
truths.details:
AttachedItems exposes a flat getItem(string) accessor but the underlying Java method is unchecked — passing a string that isn't in the character's registered AttachedLocationGroup produces a Java RuntimeException at the bridge layer, not a Lua-side nil. Symptom in logs: 'java.lang.RuntimeException: no such location <name>' with a stack trace through AttachedItems.getItem().

Safe pattern:
```lua
local attached = player:getAttachedItems()
local group = attached.getGroup and attached:getGroup()
if not group then return end
local found = false
local gi = 0
while gi < group:size() do
    local loc = group:getLocationByIndex(gi)
    if loc and loc:getId() == locationName then found = true; break end
    gi = gi + 1
end
if not found then return end
local item = attached:getItem(locationName)
```

This is the failure mode that bit FrontBackpacks in client context-menu code; the same defensive iteration is the documented fix in the FrontBackpacks_Client.lua location-guard.

truths.summary: B42 positional world sounds use getSoundManager():PlayWorldSoundImpl — define sounds in scripts/*.txt with a module namespace
truths.details: In Build 42, the correct API for triggering a positional world sound is: `getSoundManager():PlayWorldSoundImpl(name, loop, x, y, z, delay, radius, volume, ignoreWalls)`. Sound definitions must be declared in a scripts/*.txt file using a module namespace (not 'Base'). Example in media/scripts/LC_sounds.txt using the LC module namespace produces sound names like 'MZ_Scream1' and 'MZ_Scream2'. The loop parameter is boolean; delay is integer ms; radius controls falloff distance; ignoreWalls is boolean. Do not use the B41 PlayWorldSound variant — it is either removed or unreliable in B42.
evidence: Mod 3738217328 — MZ_Scream1 and MZ_Scream2 defined in media/scripts/LC_sounds.txt (LC module namespace) and played via getSoundManager():PlayWorldSoundImpl
owner-verified: owner extracted and confirmed this API pattern from direct analysis of mod 3738217328

truths.summary: In pz-temp / pz-dedicated servertest.ini, the Mods= line uses SEMICOLON (;) as the inter-mod delimiter, NOT comma. A comma-delimited list is treated as a single mod ID (e.g. Mods=A,B,C tries to load one mod called 'A,B,C' and silently fails to load A/B/C individually). Affects any multi-mod deploy script.
truths.details: Surfaced 2026-06-01 by 4.7 during SRJ Pattern A migration apply. Initial multi-mod boot attempt used 'Mods=ChuckleberryFinnAlertSystem,errorMagnifier,SkillRecoveryJournal' — server interpreted as one mod ID, none of the 3 loaded. Switching to semicolon ('Mods=A;B;C') resolved cleanly: all 3 mods loaded individually. Documents pz-dedicated config parser behavior, not yet codified in any reference. Mod-deploy scripts (manual or automated) must use ';' for multi-mod loadouts on dedicated servers.
evidence: 4.7 SRJ migration apply 2026-06-01: comma-delimited Mods= line caused all 3 mods to silently not-load; semicolon-delimited line loaded all 3 at log lines L86, L113, L116.

truths.summary: Context menu icons are set on the returned option object via option.iconTexture, not as a parameter to addOption/addOptionOnTop.
truths.details: ISContextMenu:addOption and addOptionOnTop both accept (name, target, onSelect, param1..param10) — no icon parameter exists. allocOption stores only those fields; iconTexture is initialized nil. To add an icon, capture the returned option and set option.iconTexture = getTexture(path). addOptionOnTop follows the same pattern. addColorBoxOption is a vanilla shortcut that sets iconTexture to Texture.getWhite() for a color swatch.
evidence: owner-verified: ISContextMenu.lua:849-911 (vanilla_source at Workshop/ProjectZomboid/media/lua/client/ISUI/ISContextMenu.lua): allocOption has no iconTexture param; addOption sets option.iconTexture = nil; addOptionOnTop calls allocOption with no icon handling; addColorBoxOption shows the post-call assignment pattern: option.iconTexture = Texture.getWhite().

truths.summary: OnPreFillWorldObjectContextMenu fires BEFORE vanilla entries; use it to place mod options above all vanilla context menu options.
truths.details:
If you add options in OnFillWorldObjectContextMenu they appear after vanilla entries. To place mod options above vanilla entries, subscribe to OnPreFillWorldObjectContextMenu instead.

Same parameter signature as the post-fill event:
```lua
Events.OnPreFillWorldObjectContextMenu.Add(function(playerNum, contextMenu, worldObjects, test)
    if test then return end
    local player = getSpecificPlayer(playerNum)
    if not player then return end
    -- options added here appear ABOVE vanilla entries
end)
```
evidence: B42_Lua_Events_Official.md — UI/Input Events table, OnPreFillWorldObjectContextMenu row

truths.summary: OnFillWorldObjectContextMenu receives a 'test' boolean arg — when true it is a probe pass for cursor feedback; return early to skip heavy logic.
truths.details:
The signature is `onFillWorldObjectContextMenu(playerIdx, context, worldobjects, test)`. When `test == true` the engine is probing whether any options would be added (e.g. for cursor icon feedback) — no menu will actually be displayed. Always guard:

```lua
Events.OnFillWorldObjectContextMenu.Add(function(playerIdx, context, worldobjects, test)
    if test then return end  -- probe only, skip expensive logic
    local player = getSpecificPlayer(playerIdx)  -- NOTE: first arg is INDEX not IsoPlayer
    if not player then return end
    -- add menu options
end)
```

Also: the first arg is a player INDEX (int), not an IsoPlayer — always resolve with getSpecificPlayer(playerIdx).
evidence: B42_ISUI_Components.md — Context Menu Pattern section: test parameter

truths.summary: B42 in-hand crafts should not Lua-scan bags/hands/crates. Use craftRecipe Tags=InHandCraft;CanBeDoneFromFloor so the engine includes inventory (including worn bags), hands, floor, and nearby world containers. Put item 1 [*] last. OnCreate must remove kept items via item:getContainer() plus sendRemoveItemFromContainer, not only character:getInventory():Remove. Surface-only crafts use AnySurfaceCraft instead (Hammertime curtains).
truths.details: Do not write custom getInventory/getWornItems/nearby-crate loops to feed a craftRecipe. Vanilla Handcraft/Craft UI already gathers player inventory (nested bags), equipped hands, and with CanBeDoneFromFloor nearby floor/world containers. InHandCraft alone is inventory-centric and hides crate/floor ingredients. A wildcard [*] that is not the last input steals every candidate so later typed/tag slots (DuctTape, flashlight tags) never match. mode:keep items still occupy a container; OnCreate must Remove from item:getContainer(). Worn clothing may still be excluded from the craft pool until unequipped into inventory — that is engine source-list behaviour, not a missing API call. Corpus: Hammertime htMake* curtains (AnySurfaceCraft + typed inputs, no wildcard-first). Wiki SawLogs (InHandCraft;CanBeDoneFromFloor). Authentic Z clothing convert uses getAllConsumedItems after the engine already selected inputs. CSGOAWPO has no recipes (script-only stubs).

truths.summary: craftRecipe OnTest/OnCreate are resolved by string name at USE time, not at script-parse time. If the Lua file defining the referenced function crashes anywhere above that definition, the recipe silently gets a nil OnTest/OnCreate instead of a script-load error.
truths.details: DuctTapedFlashlight_RecipeLogic.lua crashed at a top-level line (see b42.lua.shared-load-order-alphabetical-not-dependency-aware) BEFORE reaching the `function DuctTapedFlashlightRecipe.OnTest.CanAttach(...)` / `OnCreate.Attach(...)` assignments further down the same file. The .txt recipe script's `OnTest = DuctTapedFlashlightRecipe.OnTest.CanAttach` / `OnCreate = DuctTapedFlashlightRecipe.OnCreate.Attach` lines parsed fine at script-load time (script parsing does not validate that the named function actually exists) -- the game only tries to resolve and call those names when a player interacts with the recipe. At that point the table path resolved to nil. Observed effect on our recipe: a nil OnTest was treated as no restriction at all (the wildcard headwear-only input slot accepted literally any item), and a nil OnCreate meant our actual attach logic never ran -- but the recipe still visibly 'completed' and consumed its Base.DuctTape input, because base input consumption (destroy/drain per the inputs{} block) is performed by the crafting engine itself and is NOT gated on a custom OnCreate existing; OnCreate is an add-on hook, not the thing that performs consumption. Net symptom from the player's side: 'it lets me craft with anything, and afterwards nothing happened, but my tape still got used up' -- with zero recipe-specific error anywhere, only an unrelated-looking Lua crash earlier in the boot log. Takeaway for debugging: if a craftRecipe misbehaves in a way that looks like OnTest/OnCreate aren't running at all, check the boot log for ANY crash in the file that defines those functions, even if the crash's own line number/message has nothing to do with recipes.
evidence: console.txt: DuctTapedFlashlight_RecipeLogic.lua crashed at line 23, which is above every `function DuctTapedFlashlightRecipe.OnTest.*` / `OnCreate.*` assignment in that file

owner report (runtime_sp): 'its allowing me to duct tape the flashlight to everything, not just hats.. and also the flashlight functionality doesnt work' -- exactly matches nil-OnTest (unrestricted) + nil-OnCreate (logic never runs) rather than a logic bug in the OnTest/OnCreate bodies themselves

truths.summary: In a craftRecipe inputs{} block, order a wildcard `item N [*]` line LAST, after every tag[]/itemtype-constrained line -- every vanilla recipe using [*] places it last, and placing it first is suspected to let input-matching greedily bind the wildcard to an item that should satisfy a later specific-typed line.
truths.details: DuctTapedFlashlight's AttachFlashlightToHat recipe originally listed `item 1 [*] mode:keep` (the headwear slot) FIRST, before `item 1 tags[base:flashlight]` and `item 1 [Base.DuctTape]`. After fixing an unrelated Lua load-order crash (see b42.lua.shared-load-order-alphabetical-not-dependency-aware) that had been masking this, the owner reported the crafting menu no longer detected the duct tape or flashlight in inventory at all, making the recipe uncraftable, despite both items being present and both input lines using ordinary tags[]/itemtype matching with no custom OnTest involved. Every wildcard-input example found in the currently-installed 42.20.3 vanilla scripts (recipes_baking.txt: MakeCookieDough, MakeBiscuitDough, MakeCornbread, MakeBrownieBatter, etc., all using a trailing `item 1 [*]` as an optional last flavoring slot) places `[*]` as the LAST input line, never first or in the middle. Reordering our recipe to put tags[base:flashlight] and [Base.DuctTape] first and `item 1 [*] mode:keep` last is the fix applied. NOTE: this fix has been applied and passes static validation, but has not yet been independently confirmed via a live retest isolated from other changes -- the causal mechanism (wildcard greedily consuming the wrong physical item, starving a later specific-typed line of its match) is inferred from vanilla convention + the observed symptom, not confirmed against engine source. Re-verify and bump confidence to high once a live test confirms input detection works with [*] last and fails/regresses with [*] first, all else equal.
evidence: media/scripts/generated/recipes/recipes_baking.txt: every `item 1 [*]` occurrence found (5+ recipes) is the final input line in its block, after all tags[]/explicit-itemtype lines
owner report (runtime_sp, after the Lua-crash fix landed): 'now its not picking up the duct tape or flashlights on the crafting menu - therefore making it unable to craft' -- with [*] as input line 1
fix applied: reordered to tags[base:flashlight], then [Base.DuctTape], then [*] mode:keep last; static release gate PASS after reorder; live confirmation pending

truths.summary: DangerousWeather production gate BLOCK is false positives - core helpers convert Java lists, OnTick throttled, translations exist, constants used
truths.details:
DangerousWeather mod (test server/DangerousWeather) production gate shows BLOCK but all findings are FALSE POSITIVES from audit tool limitations:

1. 4 HIGH "Java ArrayList ipairs/#": Core helpers `DangerousWeatherCore.getOnlinePlayers()` and `getCharactersInSquare()` internally iterate Java ArrayLists with `:size()`/`:get(i)` and return Lua tables. Audit doesn't trace through function calls.

3. 15 LOW "missing sandbox tooltip translations": Sandbox.json HAS all 15 `_Tooltip` keys (capital T). Audit incorrectly looks for `_tooltip` (lowercase).

4. 11 LOW "dynamic command contracts": Using `DangerousWeatherCore.COMMANDS.ADMIN_TRIGGER_HAIL` constants is flagged as dynamic because audit only recognizes string literals, not table lookups from constant tables.

Code is production-ready. Audit tool needs improvement to trace helper returns, detect throttle counters, match case-sensitive keys, and resolve constant table lookups.

truths.summary: On a dedicated server, Events.OnCreatePlayer fires before the client's chargen trait selections are synchronised — hasTrait() always returns false at that point.
truths.details: When a player connects to a dedicated server, the server fires Events.OnCreatePlayer as soon as the player object is created. At this moment the client's chargen descriptor (selected traits, profession) has not yet been transmitted and applied to the server-side player object. Any hasTrait(handle) calls on that player return false regardless of what was selected in chargen. This silently skips any server-side logic that depends on trait state at spawn time (e.g. applying starting injuries). The fix is a client-detect pattern: the client checks its own traits at Events.OnGameStart (where trait data IS available locally), builds a flags table describing what needs to happen, and sends sendClientCommand(player, module, command, flags) to the server. The server command handler receives the request after full synchronisation, re-validates traits via hasTrait() as a security check, and applies the effect. Also use body-state checks (e.g. getFractureTime > 0) in both client and server to make the operation idempotent on reconnect.
evidence: applyStartingInjuries called server-side at Events.OnCreatePlayer on dedicated pz-temp; instrumented log showed hasBrokenArm=false / hasBrokenLeg=false / hasSeverelyBurned=false for every player despite traits being selected in chargen

Replacing server-side OnCreatePlayer call with client OnGameStart detection + sendClientCommand 'ApplyStartingInjuries' + server onClientCommand handler resolved the timing gap — 2026-06-09 pz-temp dedicated

truths.summary: A single invalid/removed/inaccessible Workshop ID in WorkshopItems= hard-crashes B42 dedicated server boot: Steam fails the download (result=42) and PZ's failure handler NPEs in GameServerWorkshopItems.Install (deleteDirectory(null)). One bad ID = no boot. Validate every ID before boot.
truths.details: Failure signature in the server console: 'Workshop: download 0/0 ID=<id>' + clientdll 'Staging/Install library folder not found' + 'onItemNotDownloaded itemID=<id> result=42' + 'item state DownloadPending -> Fail' followed by java.lang.NullPointerException at zombie.ZomboidFileSystem.deleteDirectory(ZomboidFileSystem.java:1478) via zombie.network.GameServerWorkshopItems.Install — then full server exit (a secondary IsoMetaGrid.save NPE during shutdown is collateral noise). Causes: typo'd ID, item deleted/removed from the Workshop, item for a different game, or visibility the server account cannot access (hidden items — unlisted items ARE downloadable by ID). Diagnosis: the failing ID is named in the log; check https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=<id> — a removed/non-PZ item confirms it. Fix: remove or correct the ID in WorkshopItems= and restart the instance. Prevention: validate every WorkshopItems ID (exists, PZ app 108600, accessible) before boot — one transcription error during modlist edits takes the whole server down.

Console showed the exact signature: result=42, DownloadPending -> Fail, NPE at ZomboidFileSystem.deleteDirectory via GameServerWorkshopItems.Install(GameServerWorkshopItems.java:248), server exit.

truths.summary: Files under media/lua/client/ load only in processes where isServer()=false (singleplayer, hosted-host player, remote client) and do NOT load in the dedicated or embedded-coop-server process. So a top-level `if not isServer() then ... end` wrapper in a client file is always-true: a redundant no-op, harmless but not a real guard.
truths.details: Reasoning (UNVERIFIED — candidate from NEGGUARD_FLAGGED_REVIEW_2026-05-31.md): client/ Lua is loaded on client processes only. Per the verified env table, the only processes that load client files are SP (isServer=false), hosted-host player (isServer=false), and remote client (isServer=false). The dedicated and embedded-coop-server processes (isServer=true) do not load client/ files at all. Therefore `if not isServer()` at the top of a client file never evaluates false in any context the file actually runs in — it always runs the body. This makes such wrappers redundant (observed in BitemeReputationClient.lua:203, BitemeReputationUI.lua:537/588). Implication: they are safe to leave OR cosmetically unwrap; they are NOT bugs. To VERIFY: deploy a client/ probe printing a load marker, boot dedicated (expect marker ABSENT) and SP (expect marker PRESENT). If confirmed, this also pins that client/ files do not execute on dedicated.
evidence: Derivation from verified env truth table + observed redundant wrappers in Biteme Mod Suite client files (NEGGUARD_FLAGGED_REVIEW_2026-05-31.md). No runtime evidence yet.

truths.summary: The embedded coop server sub-process (spawned when a player chooses Host) reports isCoopHost()==false, NOT true. By the standard env globals it is indistinguishable from a real dedicated server (isServer=true, isClient=false, isCoopHost=false, isMultiplayer=true). Confirmed B42.18.0 on local-<owner>.
truths.details:
Observed values on the embedded coop server sub-process (coop-console.txt, PZTEMP-SP-BOOT line 1184-1192, 2026-05-31T11:16):
  isServer       = true
  isClient       = false
  isCoopHost     = false   <-- naive expectation: would be true on a coop server
  isMultiplayer  = true
  isSinglePlayer = nil

Implication: code that needs to distinguish 'embedded coop server spawned by a host game' from 'standalone dedicated server' CANNOT rely on isCoopHost() inside that process. Have to either:
  - Detect via getServerOptions() / network mode / parent process
  - Detect via filesystem (does %USERPROFILE%/Zomboid/coop-console.txt     exist for this run? doesn't really help once running)
  - Just treat both as 'dedicated-class' and code accordingly.

The naming of `isCoopHost` is misleading: it's true on the host's CLIENT side (the player process), not on the host's SERVER side. Treat it as 'am I the host PLAYER' rather than 'is this a coop context'.
evidence: runtime_dedicated: coop-console.txt PZTEMP-SP-BOOT lines 1184-1192 (2026-05-31T11:16:41). isServer=TRUE, isClient=false, isCoopHost=FALSE. See docs/tracking/sp_rig_runs/HH-coopserver-2026-05-31T11-16-markers.txt
vanilla_source: needs a Java-source pin to confirm isCoopHost()'s actual definition in the engine (probably tied to the player-process model, not the server-process model).

observations: javap LuaManager$GlobalObject.isCoopHost() bytecode: getstatic GameClient.connection; ifnull -> return 0; else getfield UdpConnection.isCoopHost; -> return that boolean.

javap GameServer.main(String[]) sets server=true (offsets 15-16) and coop=true conditionally (offsets 153-154 on -coop argv). Does NOT touch GameClient.connection — the field stays at its class-init default (null).
javap GameClient.startLocalServer() (the host-player codepath) is what would assign GameClient.connection; coop sub-process never invokes it.

Implication: isCoopHost() is best read as 'am I the host PLAYER process', not 'is this a coop context'. There is currently no Lua global that distinguishes 'embedded coop server' from 'real standalone dedicated server' — both have isServer=true, isClient=false, isCoopHost=false, isMultiplayer=true.

GameServer.coop boolean IS set on the coop sub-process (per the -coop putstatic at offset 154), but it is NOT bound to a Lua global on LuaManager$GlobalObject (grep count for isCoop/coopServer/getCoop: 0 in GlobalObject.class). Worth a future binding ('isEmbeddedCoopServer()' helper) — file as Brain TODO.

truths.summary: Use positive early-return guards: client files guard with isServer(), server files guard with isClient(), and shared files usually have no guard.
truths.details: Negative guards such as if not isServer() then return end can break singleplayer and hosted-host behavior. Guard selection must follow file side, not desired feature ownership alone.

truths.summary: CONTRADICTS CLAUDE.md env truth table: the hosted-game host PLAYER process has isClient()==true (NOT false). Confirmed B42.18.0 on local-<owner>. Implication: env detection that uses 'isClient()==false AND isServer()==false' to recognise hosted-host will MISS hosted-host and tag it as SP. The reliable hosted-host signature is isCoopHost()==true (works on the host player) regardless of isClient.
truths.details:
Observed values on hosted-host PLAYER process (console.txt, PZTEMP-SP-BOOT line 906-914, 2026-05-31T11:16):
  isServer       = false
  isClient       = true   <-- CLAUDE.md says FALSE
  isCoopHost     = true
  isMultiplayer  = true
  isSinglePlayer = nil   (global absent per b42.globals.iscoophost-issinglemultiplayer)

Compare CLAUDE.md truth table:
  | Hosted game host player | isServer=false | isClient=false |

Practical impact:
1. Code with `if isClient() then return end` in shared/-folder files WILL skip on hosted-host's host player (because isClient=true). Authors who used that as a 'server-side intent' guard get expected behaviour on the host player (skipped) and the wanted execution on the coop sub-process (where isClient=false). So this guard works correctly - the CLAUDE.md table description is just wrong about WHY.

truths.summary: Negative env guards (`if not isClient() and not isServer() then return end`) break singleplayer (both false → returns early) and misbehave on hosted-host (isClient=true → continues, but for wrong reasons). Correct server guard: `if isClient() then return end`.

truths.summary: Mods can declare custom events with LuaEventManager.AddEvent('Name') and trigger them with Events.Name.trigger(args); same .Add/.Remove API as engine events.
truths.details:
Pattern for decoupled inter-module communication within a mod:

```lua
-- Shared file, loaded once:
LuaEventManager.AddEvent('MyMod_OnDataReady')

-- Subscribe anywhere:
Events.MyMod_OnDataReady.Add(function(data)
    -- handle data
end)

-- Trigger from another module:
Events.MyMod_OnDataReady.trigger(myData)
```

The same .Add/.Remove/.trigger API applies as for all engine events. AddEvent is idempotent if called multiple times with the same name. Custom events are indistinguishable from engine events at runtime.

truths.summary: OnInitGlobalModData fires with a newGame (bool) parameter on both client and server; use the newGame branch for fresh-save initialization.
truths.details:
Signature: `function onInitGlobalModData(newGame)`. It is a Shared event so it fires on both client and server.

The newGame boolean distinguishes fresh saves from loaded saves, allowing different initialization paths:

```lua
Events.OnInitGlobalModData.Add(function(newGame)
    local md = ModData.getOrCreate('MyMod')
    if newGame then
        -- fresh world: set defaults
        md.version = 1
        md.data = {}
        ModData.transmit('MyMod')
    else
        -- existing save: validate/migrate
        if not md.version then
            md.version = 1
            ModData.transmit('MyMod')
        end
    end
end)
```

This is the canonical hook for server ModData bootstrap (per CLAUDE.md). Environment guards still apply — client-side code should skip heavy init.

truths.summary: `Events.OnPlayerSayCommand` is null in singleplayer AND on hosted-host AND on c2d client. Calling `.Add(fn)` on it crashes with 'attempted index: Add of non-table: null'. Always guard: `if Events.OnPlayerSayCommand then Events.OnPlayerSayCommand.Add(fn) end`. The event only exists on the DEDICATED SERVER process when a client is connected — it does NOT exist on the client side in any observed environment.
truths.details:
Events.OnPlayerSayCommand is a client-only chat-routing event that is populated by the multiplayer client subsystem at session-start. In environments where there is no MP client session (singleplayer; hosted_host where the host is server-side from a routing perspective), the event entry is null/absent from the Events table. The standard Lua pattern Events.X.Add(fn) therefore attempts to index nil, crashing the entire module load with a Kahlua error: 'attempted index: Add of non-table: null'.

The asymmetry per environment matches the env-guard truth table (see b42.env.guards.positive / T1):
- sp:                  Events.OnPlayerSayCommand = null  → unguarded .Add CRASHES
- hosted_host:         Events.OnPlayerSayCommand = null  → unguarded .Add CRASHES
- hosted_client:       Events.OnPlayerSayCommand exists  → .Add OK
- dedicated:           N/A — client-side event; dedicated does not load client files
- client_to_dedicated: Events.OnPlayerSayCommand exists  → .Add OK

Safe pattern:
```lua
if Events.OnPlayerSayCommand then
    Events.OnPlayerSayCommand.Add(myChatHandler)
end
```

This is one of several events that follow the 'null-in-some-environments' pattern; see also b42.events.everytenseconds-nil-dedicated (the dedicated-side analog).

Original truth wording: 'null in singleplayer'. C2D session 2026-05-31 23:45 observed that `Events.OnPlayerSayCommand.type` is ALSO nil on c2d client at both load-time AND post-OnGameStart:

  - Hosted-host player (original)
  - **c2d client** (NEW, 2026-06-01 observation)

Only context where the event is non-nil (table): DEDICATED SERVER
process with at least one client connected.

Mod-author implication: any client-side or SP code that wants to react to chat-commands needs an alternative mechanism (OnPlayerUpdate + polling player text, or hook a different chat event). The OnPlayerSayCommand event is a server-only construct on B42.18.

truths.summary: OnZombieUpdate fires once per zombie per frame for active-cell zombies; gate expensive sub-tasks with a modulo tick counter and Remove-before-Add to prevent double registration.
truths.details:
OnZombieUpdate is the correct hook for per-NPC AI logic (Bandits V2 drives its entire AI brain off it). Because it fires every frame per active zombie it can be high-frequency:

```lua
local function onZombieUpdate(zombie)
    -- Gate expensive work to every 10th frame
    zombie.myMod_tick = (zombie.myMod_tick or 0) + 1
    if zombie.myMod_tick % 10 ~= 0 then return end
    
    -- expensive AI logic here
end

-- Prevent double-registration on file reload:
Events.OnZombieUpdate.Remove(onZombieUpdate)
Events.OnZombieUpdate.Add(onZombieUpdate)
```

The Remove-before-Add pattern prevents duplicate handlers accumulating if the file is re-required.

truths.summary: player:getAccessLevel() returns both 'Admin'/'admin' and 'Moderator'/'moderator' casings — always check both; solo players should be treated as admin via isSinglePlayer().
truths.details:
PZ has historically returned both casings for Admin and Moderator roles. Safe guard:

```lua
local function isAdmin(player)
    if isSinglePlayer() then return true end  -- solo always admin in UI gates
    local level = player:getAccessLevel()
    return level == 'admin' or level == 'Admin'
end

local function isModerator(player)
    local level = player:getAccessLevel()
    return level == 'moderator' or level == 'Moderator'
        or level == 'admin' or level == 'Admin'
end
```

Empty string `""` means a default (non-privileged) player. Other valid values: `"Overseer"`, `"GM"`, `"Observer"`. For solo play, use isSinglePlayer() for UI gates rather than calling getAccessLevel() to ensure SP players see admin controls.

truths.summary: On B42.18 dedicated, `player:getAccessLevel()` returns the string 'animal' for connected players who are NOT in the server's admin / moderator / observer list. This is a new (unanticipated) access level string beyond the documented Admin/Moderator/Observer set, and it does NOT match the dual-casing pattern in `b42.globals.accesslevel-dual-casing`. Mod authors checking accesslevel for permissions must include 'animal' as a possible non-privileged value.
truths.details:
## Observation

C2D session 2026-05-31 23:45: user 'Space' (Mr Space Cadet's account) connected to pz-temp via Multiplayer→Join (no password set on this instance) and PZTempMP_Client probed `player:getAccessLevel()` at OnGameStart. The returned value was the literal string `'animal'`.

```
PZTEMP-MP-CL|target.accesslevel|player.getAccessLevel.val|animal
PZTEMP-MP-CL|target.accesslevel|ctx|c2d_or_hc_client
```

## Interpretation

Two possibilities (need further probing to distinguish):

1. **'animal' is the default access level for non-privileged players** on B42.18 — a new sentinel string the engine uses when the connecting account has no admin/moderator/observer rights. If true, mod authors checking accesslevel must treat 'animal' as equivalent to 'none' / empty / unprivileged.

2. **'Space' account on pz-temp wasn't in the admin list** at session time (Password='' so open-access; admin list lives in the per-instance SQLite db, not visible in servertest.ini). Need to verify by either (a) running `/grantadmin Space` and reconnecting to compare, or (b) inspecting the player-records db directly.

## Mitigation pattern (regardless of root cause)

```lua
local level = player:getAccessLevel()
local low   = level and level:lower() or 'none'
local is_admin = (low == 'admin')
local is_mod   = (low == 'moderator')
local is_obs   = (low == 'observer')
local is_nonpriv = (low == 'animal' or low == 'none' or low == '' or not level)
```

## Cross-reference

- `b42.globals.accesslevel-dual-casing` — original dual-casing claim; does NOT mention 'animal' as a possible return value.
- This truth supplements rather than supersedes the dual-casing truth; both can be true (Admin/admin OR Moderator/moderator OR animal as the default-non-privileged sentinel).

truths.summary: Frame-rate-normalize per-frame countdowns using getAverageFPS(); formula: time = time - 1/((getAverageFPS()+0.5)*0.01666667).
truths.details:
When a per-frame handler ticks down a wall-clock duration, use getAverageFPS() to normalize so the countdown is independent of frame rate:

```lua
local timeRemaining = 5.0  -- 5 seconds

local function onTick()
    local fps = getAverageFPS()
    timeRemaining = timeRemaining - 1.0 / ((fps + 0.5) * 0.01666667)
    if timeRemaining <= 0 then
        Events.OnTick.Remove(onTick)
        doSomething()
    end
end
Events.OnTick.Add(onTick)
```

Formula source: Bandits V2 BanditUpdate.lua. Also: getRandomUUID() provides stable engine-generated UUIDs suitable as persistent record keys.

truths.summary: readFromFile() and writeToFile() are NOT top-level Lua globals on B42.18 dedicated. Use getFileWriter(name, append, force) for writes and the engine-managed file-reader paths for reads. Confirmed by V3b 2026-05-31 dedicated probe (api.readFromFile=absent, api.writeToFile=absent at shared-load on fresh-vanilla boot).
truths.details:
These two function names appear in pre-B42 mod documentation but are absent from the B42.18 LuaManager$GlobalObject exposed surface on dedicated. Authors should use:

Writes:
  local fw = getFileWriter('myfile.txt', true, false)
  if fw then
    fw:write(line)
    fw:close()
  end

truths.summary: Render3DItem() silently no-ops outside Events.RenderOpaqueObjectsInWorld — must not be called from OnTick, OnRenderTick, OnPostRender, or OnPostUIDraw.
truths.details:
The world render context is only active inside Events.RenderOpaqueObjectsInWorld handlers. Calling Render3DItem() from any other event silently does nothing with no error.

Correct usage:
```lua
Events.RenderOpaqueObjectsInWorld.Add(function()
    local player = getSpecificPlayer(0)
    if not player then return end
    local zoom = getCore():getZoom(0)  -- fetch once per render pass
    
    -- item can be a temporary instanceItem never placed in world
    local item = instanceItem('Base.MyItem')
    item:setWorldAlpha(0.8)
    item:setWorldScale(zoom)
    Render3DItem(item, square, x, y, z, yaw)
end)
```

truths.summary: Use triggerEvent('OnServerCommand', module, cmd, args) in singleplayer to let one OnServerCommand handler serve both SP and MP without a code fork.
truths.details:
In singleplayer there is no server, so sendClientCommand does nothing. The unification pattern: in SP call triggerEvent to synthetically fire the same event that the MP path receives via sendClientCommand:

```lua
local function sendCommand(module, cmd, args)
    local isSPOrHost = not isClient() and not isServer()
    if isSPOrHost then
        -- Simulate the server receiving the command directly
        triggerEvent('OnServerCommand', module, cmd, args)
    else
        sendClientCommand(module, cmd, args)
    end
end

-- One handler serves both paths:
Events.OnServerCommand.Add(function(module, cmd, args)
    if module ~= 'MyMod' then return end
    -- handle cmd
end)
```

triggerEvent is equivalent to Events.<Name>.trigger(...).

truths.summary: Always null the singleton reference in ISCollapsableWindow:close() override to prevent stale panel references on reopen.
truths.details:
When using a singleton pattern for mod panels (one global instance), the close() override must nil the reference:

```lua
local instance = nil

function MyPanel:close()
    ISCollapsableWindow.close(self)  -- call parent first
    instance = nil  -- REQUIRED: clear singleton
end

function MyPanel.toggle()
    if instance then
        instance:close()
    else
        instance = MyPanel.new()
        instance:initialise()
        instance:addToUIManager()
    end
end
```

Failing to nil the singleton causes subsequent open attempts to reuse or partially reinitialize the stale panel, resulting in invisible panels or incorrect state.
evidence: B42_ISUI_Components.md — ISCollapsableWindow Lifecycle Methods table, close() row

truths.summary: Set self.moveWithMouse = true on an ISPanel to enable built-in user dragging with no custom mouse handlers needed.
truths.details:
ISPanel has a built-in drag mechanism. Setting `o.moveWithMouse = true` in the :new() constructor makes the panel user-draggable without writing onMouseMove/onMouseDown/onMouseUp handlers:

```lua
function MyPanel.new(x, y, w, h)
    local o = ISPanel:new(x, y, w, h)
    o.moveWithMouse = true  -- enables built-in drag
    return o
end
```

To persist position after a drag, override :onMouseUp, call the parent `ISPanel.onMouseUp(self, x, y)` first, then save `self:getX()` / `self:getY()` to ModData.
evidence: B42_ISUI_Components.md — ISPanel Built-in Drag section

truths.summary: Accumulating 30+ vanilla ISUI requires in a single mod file corrupts Kahlua's callFrame stack and causes all timed actions to crash with ReturnValues NPE.
truths.details:
In B42, ISUI classes (ISPanel, ISButton, etc.) are pre-loaded globals — require statements for them are optional. A production incident confirmed that 30+ `require 'ISUI/...'` calls in one file overflowed Kahlua's callFrame stack, causing every timed action to crash with a ReturnValues NPE.

Rules:
- Keep requires minimal — never require ISUI/* classes that are already globals
- Never use require inside a function body
- Place any necessary requires at the very top of the file only

truths.summary: Java inner classes are exposed to Lua on B42.18 dedicated via TWO valid access forms: (1) Outer.Inner dot-notation from the outer-class table (e.g. ServerOptions.BooleanServerOption), and (2) bare 'Inner' as a top-level _G global (e.g. BooleanServerOption directly). The ORIGINAL `_G['Outer$Inner']` claim was WRONG — $ is NOT preserved in the Lua-side keys. Use dot-notation or bare-top-level access; avoid the legacy _G['Outer$Inner'] pattern.
truths.details:
## Verified access patterns (B42.18 dedicated, T38 probe)

Both of these work, pick the one that's most readable:

```lua
-- Form 1: Outer.Inner dot-notation
local BoolOpt   = ServerOptions.BooleanServerOption
local IntOpt    = ServerOptions.IntegerServerOption
local EnumSand  = SandboxOptions.EnumSandboxOption
local PerksTbl  = PerkFactory.Perks
local XP        = IsoGameCharacter.XP

-- Form 2: bare 'Inner' as top-level global
local BoolOpt   = BooleanServerOption        -- same table as ServerOptions.BooleanServerOption
local EnumSand  = EnumSandboxOption          -- same table as SandboxOptions.EnumSandboxOption
local PerksTbl  = Perks                      -- same table as PerkFactory.Perks
```

## Anti-pattern (does NOT work)

```lua
-- WRONG: $ is not preserved in Lua-side keys on B42.18
local BoolOpt = _G['ServerOptions$BooleanServerOption']  -- returns nil
```

## Coverage notes

- Not every inner class is exposed both ways. LuaManager itself is NOT exposed as a global, so neither LuaManager.Exposer nor a bare Exposer global exists. Use Form 1 only when you've confirmed the outer class is a Lua-visible global.
- 22 'inner-like' bare-named globals exist in _G (matching patterns like *Option, *Inner, XP) — sample: ConfigOption, BooleanConfigOption, StringConfigOption, DoubleConfigOption, IntegerConfigOption, BooleanDebugOption, BooleanServerOption, StringServerOption, TextServerOption, IntegerServerOption, DoubleServerOption, XP.
- Total _G key count on a vanilla B42.18 dedicated boot: **2297 keys**.

## Reflection-based access NOT available

- `luautils.classFromName` does NOT exist on `luautils` (method absent).
- `java.lang.Class.forName` is not reachable as a Lua global.

## Origin of the original mistake

The original truth was derived from the JAR layout: `jar tf projectzomboid.jar | grep '$'` shows inner-class `.class` files preserving the `$` (e.g. `zombie/characters/IsoGameCharacter$XP.class`). Lua-side exposure DROPS the `$` separator — the JVM-level file naming and the Lua-level key naming use different conventions. The lua-exposed-java-bindings.md catalog should be updated to reflect the dot-notation / bare-name forms.

Access path: _G['Outer$Inner'] (not Outer.Inner or Outer$Inner direct)
Affects any nested-class Java type bound to Lua

truths.summary: next() is NOT exposed as a global in PZ B42 Kahlua. Calling next(t) throws java.lang.RuntimeException: "Object tried to call nil". Use pairs-based iteration or a tablelength()-style counter for empty/non-empty table checks instead. pairs() IS available; next() is not.
truths.details: Kahlua (PZ's Lua VM) does not register the standard Lua 5.1 global `next` in the sandboxed mod environment, even though `pairs`/`ipairs` are available. Any direct `next(t)` call (e.g. the common `if next(t) ~= nil then` empty-table idiom) compiles fine (static Lua syntax check passes) but throws 'Object tried to call nil' at runtime the moment that line executes. Safe replacements: (a) a helper that counts via `for _ in pairs(t) do ... end`, e.g. an existing tablelength()-style function; (b) inline `local any=false; for _ in pairs(t) do any=true; break end`. This is a static-undetectable / runtime-only trap, so it is missed by luac and MCP static audits and only surfaces on a probe/live boot.
evidence: runtime_client_to_dedicated: Crash captured 2026-06-08 on the BiteMe pz-temp DEDICATED server with the owner connected as a client. java.lang.RuntimeException 'Object tried to call nil in onTick' with stack trace Lua((MOD:BB Common Sense Containers)).onTick(BB_CSContainers_HighlightFavorites.lua:239) via zombie.gameStates.IngameState.onTick; shutdown log showed UdpEngine thread termination, confirming a networked client_to_dedicated session. The only callable token on line 239 was next(highlighted) in the idiom `if next(highlighted) ~= nil then`. Error fired every tick while the feature was disabled.

Fix verified: replacing `next(highlighted) ~= nil` with `tablelength(highlighted) > 0` (a pairs-based counter) eliminated the crash; space_validate_lua_syntax passed both before and after, confirming this is runtime-only and undetectable by static checks.
Brain check 2026-06-08 (agent 46): neither space_search_brain nor space_truth_search(kind=trap) had any existing entry for next() being unavailable in Kahlua prior to this proposal.

truths.summary: Log floods with AntiCheatHitShortDistance ClassCastException are a vanilla B42 bug, not a mod bug — filter them out when diagnosing real issues.

truths.summary: `if obj.method then` is UNRELIABLE as a Java method existence guard in B42 — Kahlua reflection returns a truthy accessor object for ABSENT Java methods. Failure only surfaces on invocation, not on the presence check. Verify method existence via brain/decompiled source, not runtime guards.
truths.details:
In B42's Kahlua Lua bridge, accessing `obj.someMethod` on a Java object does NOT return nil for non-existent methods. Instead, Kahlua returns a truthy accessor/proxy object so that `if obj.someMethod then` evaluates to true even when `someMethod` does not exist on the underlying Java class.

The error is deferred to call time: `obj:someMethod()` then throws 'No implementation found for someMethod(...)' or similar. This means the idiomatic Lua nil-guard:
```lua
if obj.someMethod then obj:someMethod() end  -- WRONG: always true for Java objects
```
...gives a false sense of safety and will never skip the call.

Correct approach: verify method existence via the brain's decompiled source (javap output, _exposed_classes.txt, _exp_v.txt) or the Brain API docs, not by runtime `if obj.method then` guards. Runtime guards on Java objects are valid ONLY for entire globals (`if SomeJavaGlobal then`) or Lua-table members, not for methods on Java instances.

Basis: MED1 (BB_CommonSense_Medical) B42.19 investigation — presence checks on IsoGameCharacter methods passed but invocations failed.
evidence: MED1 (BB_CommonSense_Medical) B42.19 investigation: `if player.hasTrait then` returned truthy; `player:hasTrait(string)` then threw 'No implementation found' — demonstrating the guard gave false positive
Kahlua bridge design: Java method lookup on object access returns a method-accessor even for absent methods; exception raised at invoke, not at property access
Confirmed independently in multiple B42 MasterySystem debugging sessions where `if obj.method then` guards failed to prevent invocation errors

observations: MasterySystem SP probe 2026-06-05: traits grant+replace working — confirmed by switching all IsoGameCharacter method access to handle-based API (CharacterTrait.get + getCharacterTraits():add) after `if player.hasTrait then` guard gave false positive and invocation threw; SP boot zero Mastery errors

truths.summary: A Lua module written as `local X = {} ... return X` does NOT populate _G. Any file referencing the bare name X without a `local X = require "Path/Module"` binding gets nil, not the module table.
truths.details: In PZ B42, MasteryCommit was require()d only in server/MasteryCommands.lua (behind isClient() guard) and never in client/UI/ISMasteryPanel.lua. On client and SP, both MasteryCommit and MasteryStore resolved to nil. The ISMasteryPanel submitNode guard ('commit API not loaded') and emptyStoreView fallback masked the nil rather than crashing, making the bug invisible to casual testing. Root cause: module-local pattern with bare-global reference in a context that never loaded the module.

Lua 5.1 semantics: local variables do not populate _G. require() returns the module return value to the caller's local; a subsequent file sees _G[name] == nil unless the module explicitly set it.

truths.summary: media/lua/shared/*.lua files load in filename-alphabetical order, not dependency order. Reading another file's shared-table globals at top-level scope crashes if that file sorts later.
truths.details: Built DuctTapedFlashlight with DuctTapedFlashlight_Shared.lua (defines the mod's global table + constants) plus DuctTapedFlashlight_AttachedLocations.lua and DuctTapedFlashlight_RecipeLogic.lua, both of which read DuctTapedFlashlight.SLOT_NAME etc. at plain top-level scope. 'AttachedLocations' and 'RecipeLogic' both sort alphabetically before 'Shared', so both files executed before Shared.lua had created the DuctTapedFlashlight table, crashing every boot with 'attempted index: SLOT_NAME of non-table: null' at line 11 and line 23 respectively (Kahlua RuntimeException, KahluaThread.tableget). Both files aborted at that line, so nothing defined below it (including the recipe's OnTest/OnCreate function assignments) ever ran -- see b42.craftrecipe.ontest-oncreate-resolve-lazily-by-name for the downstream effect. Fix: (1) never read another shared file's globals at plain top-level scope -- only inside function bodies that run later, at actual gameplay time, when all mod Lua has finished loading; (2) for one-time boot registration side effects that must run at file scope (e.g. AttachedLocations group registration), wrap them in Events.OnGameBoot.Add(function() ... end), which is guaranteed to fire only after every mod's Lua has loaded, regardless of filename order.

truths.summary: PZ auto-loads .lua files only at the root of client/, server/, and shared/. Files in any subdirectory (e.g. shared/Mastery/*.lua) are NOT loaded automatically and must be pulled in with an explicit require.
truths.details: The PZ Kahlua loader walks the three canonical roots (media/lua/client, media/lua/server, media/lua/shared) and loads every .lua file found directly in those directories. It does NOT recurse into subdirectories. Any file placed in a subdirectory (shared/Mastery/, client/UI/subpanel/, etc.) is invisible to the auto-loader and will only execute when an already-loaded file require()s it. Failure to require a subdir module results in a nil global reference — not a load error — so the bug is silent until the nil is called.
evidence: MasterySystem bug 2026-06-04: ISMasteryPanel.lua referenced bare globals MasteryCommit and MasteryStore, both local-return modules in shared/Mastery/. Neither was auto-loaded in client/SP context; both resolved to nil. Fix: added require 'Mastery/MasteryStore' and require 'Mastery/MasteryCommit' at top of ISMasteryPanel.lua.

truths.summary: ModData.getOrCreate(key) returns the SAME Lua table instance on repeated calls within a session (rawequal == true). ModData.transmit(key) on dedicated is SAFE to call with ZERO connected clients - it returns cleanly, does not NPE. Both confirmed B42.18.0 dedicated runtime.
truths.details:
Both findings are pinned by the V3b dedicated probe (2026-05-31 fresh-vanilla pz-temp boot, run_log docs/tracking/PZ42_T25_V3B_RUN_2026-05-31.txt).

## Identity preservation
After:
```lua
local md1 = ModData.getOrCreate('Foo')
md1.counter = 1
local md2 = ModData.getOrCreate('Foo')
rawequal(md1, md2)  -- true; md2 IS md1
md2.counter         -- 1 (same value, same table)
```

Practical impact: mod authors can call getOrCreate freely without worrying about table-copy semantics. Writes via any handle to the same key are immediately visible via any other handle. Hold-a-reference patterns work as expected.

## transmit() safety with zero clients
On a dedicated server with NO connected clients, ModData.transmit('Foo') is safe to call - it returns cleanly without throwing. The internal packet enqueue handles the no-recipients case.

Practical impact: server-side mods that periodically transmit ModData can call transmit() unconditionally without first checking `getNumActivePlayers() > 0`. Useful for auto-save / scheduled-sync patterns.

## Caveats
- Identity preservation is per-PROCESS, not per-save. If the server restarts, in-memory ModData tables are rebuilt from disk; the new tables won't rawequal the pre-restart ones.
- transmit() safety is for the EMPTY-client case. With clients connected, transmit() obviously sends real packets and is subject to normal network failure modes.
- Not yet probed: behaviour with malformed key (nil / empty string / very long string), behaviour under concurrent OnTick + transmit, behaviour after the underlying table is set to a primitive.
