truths.summary: Held weapon orientation is controlled by the **Bip01_Prop2** attachment block in the model script (NOT Bip01_Prop1 as previously documented — T40 v2 confirms zero vanilla weapons declare Bip01_Prop1, all 6 probed vanilla weapons use Bip01_Prop2). The `world` attachment only affects ground-drop appearance. ModelRotationY/Z in item scripts affect sprite/icon display only and do not rotate the 3D held model. PZ may accept either Bip01_Prop1 or Bip01_Prop2 as a held-grip attachment (user's mods historically used Prop1 and worked) but the vanilla canonical attachment name is **Bip01_Prop2** — new model scripts should match vanilla convention.
truths.details:
## The actual vanilla pattern (B42.18, T40 v2 runtime-confirmed)

PZ holds items using the **Bip01_Prop2** bone attachment point. The model
block in a .txt script must define this attachment explicitly with the
desired rotation + offset. The `attachment world` block is a separate
declaration used only when the item is lying on the ground as a world object.
`ModelRotationY` and `ModelRotationZ` in the item script definition affect
sprite/icon display only and do not rotate the 3D held model.

## Bip01_Prop1 vs Bip01_Prop2 — empirical state on B42.18

| Weapon class | Has Bip01_Prop1 | Has Bip01_Prop2 | Bip01_Prop2 rotate (X, Y, Z) |
|---|---|---|---|
| FireAxe (Base.Axe) | NO | YES | (180, -86.03, 180) |
| HuntingKnife / Knife model | NO | YES | (0, -82.59, 2.901) |
| Handgun03 (Base.Pistol) | NO | YES | (90, 1.196, -90.04) |
| BaseballBat (2-handed) | NO | YES | (0, 0, 0) |
| Hammer | NO | YES | (0, -86.91, 0) |

ZERO vanilla weapons declare `Bip01_Prop1`. The previous truth wording —
which described Bip01_Prop1 as the primary-hand attachment and Bip01_Prop2
as the secondary/two-handed left-hand grip — is **not borne out by vanilla
weapon scripts**. All 6 probed weapons (mix of 1H and 2H) use Bip01_Prop2 as
the single held attachment.

## Mr Space Cadet's prior mod work (cross-evidence)

The user's Madness Scrap Weapons fix (2026-05-27) added `Bip01_Prop1` to 5
weapons (ChainBat, SalvagedShiv, GlassShiv, ScrapClub, SalvagedClub) and
those weapons held correctly in-game. This strongly suggests PZ's model
loader accepts EITHER `Bip01_Prop1` OR `Bip01_Prop2` as a held-grip
attachment — the engine resolves whichever is present. But the vanilla
canonical convention is **Bip01_Prop2**, and matching vanilla maximises
interop with other mods that might inspect or duplicate the attachment
structure.

## Recommended modder pattern (B42.18)

When authoring a new weapon model script, define **Bip01_Prop2** with the
desired rotation/offset (matching vanilla convention):

```text
attachment Bip01_Prop2
{
    offset = -0.0067 -0.0091 -0.0022,
    rotate = 0 0 0,
}
```

Other attachments are optional and serve specific purposes:
- `world` — ground-drop appearance (always declare for items that can be dropped)
- `muzzle` / `reddot` / `gunlight` / `scope` / `laser` — firearm-specific
  attachment points for muzzle flash, sights, accessories (see Handgun03 for
  the canonical example)

## Iteration / inspection API

The ModelScript class on B42.18 dedicated exposes ONLY `getAttachment(int)`
— there is no by-name lookup (`getAttachmentByName`/`getAttachments` are
absent). Mods that want to read attachment data must iterate by integer
index:

```lua
local ms = getScriptManager():getModelScript("Knife")
for i = 0, 15 do
    local att = ms:getAttachment(i)
    if not att then break end
    if att:getId() == "Bip01_Prop2" then
        local rot = att:getRotate()  -- userdata Vector3-like
        local off = att:getOffset()
        -- ...
    end
end
```

Model scripts are parsed once at PZ startup; a full quit-to-desktop and
relaunch is required after any model-block change to take effect.
evidence: Verified 2026-05-27 fixing 5 Madness Scrap Weapons (ChainBat, SalvagedShiv, GlassShiv, ScrapClub, SalvagedClub) via module_SWBase.txt: adding 'attachment Bip01_Prop1 { rotate = 0 0 180 }' corrected upside-down held orientation; prior edits to 'attachment world' and ModelRotationY/Z fields had no effect.
If Bip01_Prop1 block is absent from a model definition, PZ falls back to the raw FBX mesh orientation.
Two-handed weapons need Bip01_Prop2 for the secondary (left) hand grip point.
Standard correction for meshes exported upside-down relative to PZ hand bone frame: rotate = 0 0 180 (Z-axis 180 degrees).
Model scripts are parsed once at PZ startup; a full quit-to-desktop and relaunch is required after any model block change.

truths.summary: PZ MP validates the client's BASE-GAME media/lua/ files against the server's by per-file checksum at connect (a separate, LATER step than checkmods). ANY server-side modification of a vanilla file, OR any EXTRA file dropped under the server's vanilla media/lua/ tree, force-disconnects every joining client with 'checksum-File doesn't match the one on the server: <file>' or 'the file doesn't exist on the client: <file>'. Never deploy probes/test-hooks/mods by editing or dropping files into a dedicated server's vanilla game install -- use a proper mod (Mods=/Workshop), which is checksummed as a mod the client also has. The vanilla media/lua/ tree must stay byte-identical to stock for the running build.
truths.details: The check surfaces ONE file at a time, so file-by-file cleanup is whack-a-mole and the next stray file fails on the next join. Definitive recovery: `diff -rq` the server's media/lua/ against a known-STOCK install of the SAME build (e.g. a sibling instance), back up then REMOVE all extra files and RESTORE all modified files to stock until diff returns zero. World mods loaded via Mods=/Workshop live in a separate dir and are fine -- only the vanilla media/lua/ tree must stay stock. checkmods passing does NOT mean the join will succeed; the vanilla-file checksum is a distinct gate after it.
evidence: owner-verified 2026-06-06, runtime_client_to_dedicated: client could not join pz-temp despite checkmods passing. Sequential force-disconnects: 'checksum-File doesn't match the one on the server: media/lua/server/clientcommands.lua' then 'the file doesn't exist on the client: media/lua/server/pztempbattery.lua'. Root cause: prior probe sessions had injected 13 PZTemp probe scripts (T13-T33, Battery) + appended a require to ClientCommands.lua (+93 bytes) + left 19 stray .bak files in the vanilla media/lua/server/.

Fixed by diff -rq vs pz-live stock (same build 42.19.0), backing up + removing extras + restoring stock (diff_exit:0, zero differences). Docs: docs/tracking/PZTEMP_PROBE_DEPOLLUTION_2026-06-06.md, PZTEMP_CLIENTCOMMANDS_RESTORE_2026-06-06.md.

truths.summary: On dedicated server or hosted-coop, applying body damage from a CLIENT Lua file is silently overridden by the next server sync. All body-damage writes for spawn effects must be made on the SERVER process to be authoritative.
truths.details: In a B42 multiplayer session, the server owns all IsoGameCharacter body-damage state. Any writes made client-side are local only and get overwritten when the server next transmits authoritative state. This applies even at Events.OnNewGame or OnGameStart on the client — the writes simply don't persist. The cleanest solution for chargen-trait-driven spawn injuries is Events.OnNewGame in a SHARED file with 'if isClient() then return end' — this runs on the server process, writes body damage authoritatively, and requires no round-trip. See companion truth b42.event.onnewgame.spawn-injuries-shared.

Do NOT perform network ops in an OnInitGlobalModData handler: set up ModData only; clients pull config via ModData.request on join; do per-player work lazily or on a later event (OnPlayerConnected / EveryOneMinute).

truths.summary: To give a worn/attached (non-handheld) item vanilla-compatible hands-free light with a working 'Turn On/Off Light Source' keybind and free MP sync: physically move the light item into a custom character AttachedItems slot via character:setAttachedItem(), not into a clothing/ModData hack.
truths.details: Goal: a flashlight duct-taped to a hat should light up hands-free and respond to the normal light-toggle key, without writing a custom light-rendering system. Read vanilla's media/lua/server/Items/ItemBindingHandler.lua (the actual 'Turn On/Off Light Source' keybind handler): after checking playerObj:getSecondaryHandItem() and getPrimaryHandItem(), it falls through to `local attachedItems = playerObj:getAttachedItems(); for i=1,attachedItems:size() do local item = attachedItems:getItemByIndex(i-1); if item:canEmitLight() and ... then item:setActivated(not item:isActivated()); syncItemFields(playerObj, item); item:playActivateDeactivateSound() end end` -- i.e. vanilla already treats getAttachedItems() as an equal light-source candidate pool alongside the two hand slots, with the exact same activation toggle and the same syncItemFields MP-sync call. This is CONFIRMED source-read, high confidence, and is the reason no custom light code was written for DuctTapedFlashlight: implementation is (1) register a new location on `AttachedLocations.getGroup("Human"):getOrCreateLocation(slotName):setAttachmentName(boneAttachmentId)` (pattern taken from the working, currently-supported 'Simple Flashlight on Belt' mod's SFoB_AttachedLocations.lua), (2) add a matching `model FemaleBody/MaleBody { attachment <boneAttachmentId> { bone=Bip01_Head (or whichever bone), offset=..., rotate=... } }` script block (same mod's SFoB_Attachments.txt shows the syntax; an existing 'on_mining_helmet_middle' head-bone point in that mod's model block was reused as a starting coordinate guess for a head-mounted torch), (3) move the item with `character:getInventory():Remove(item); character:setAttachedItem(slotName, item); item:setAttachedSlot(-1); item:setAttachedSlotType(slotType); item:setAttachedToModel(slotName); syncItemFields(character, item)` -- API confirmed via media/lua/shared/TimedActions/ISAttachItemHotbar.lua's :perform(), which does the identical sequence for holstered/belt items. WHAT IS NOT YET CONFIRMED (hence medium, not high, confidence): whether the item visually/functionally emits light in live gameplay once attached this way -- only that the KEYBIND mechanism treats it as eligible. The item-move mechanism itself was also blocked by an unrelated bug for the first two live tests (see b42.lua.shared-load-order-alphabetical-not-dependency-aware and b42.craftrecipe.wildcard-input-should-be-last), so end-to-end light emission has not yet been observed working. Re-verify and bump to high once a live test confirms the F-key toggle actually lights the world from this slot.

truths.summary: When wrapping/overriding a vanilla method, set a sentinel field on the patched table itself (e.g. Class.__mod_x_patched=true) and bail if already set BEFORE capturing the original function; a guard stored on the patched object (not a module-local) survives require re-execution and prevents recursive double-wrapping.
truths.details: Module-level override code can run more than once across reloads or cross-mod requires. If the original is captured a second time after the first wrap, the captured 'original' is already the wrapper, producing infinite recursion. CSR_Fundamentals guards with a flag on the patched class table; BB uses a module-local boolean in some files and no guard at all in at least one vehicle hook. Prefer the on-table sentinel everywhere; it is also visible to other mods that may patch the same surface.

truths.summary: A mod built for dedicated/client that uses a sendClientCommand->OnServerCommand sync round-trip will HANG in singleplayer (UI stuck 'awaiting server sync'), because SP has no separate server process to answer the request. Fix WITHOUT splitting into two mods: make the sync env-aware. In SP/hosted-host/dedicated the server logic runs in the SAME Lua VM (isClient()==false) -> call the server-side sync function directly and populate the client cache synchronously, skipping the network wait. Only do the round-trip + 'awaiting' state for a true remote client (isClient()==true).
truths.details: Surfaced 2026-06-01 by MasterySystem SP test: panel opened (after forward-ref fix) but showed 'awaiting server sync' indefinitely in SP. The mod's requestSync sendClientCommands the server and waits for an OnServerCommand reply that never arrives in SP. Per the verified env table (b42.env.guards.positive / b42.env.hosted-host-player-isclient-true): SP=isServer false/isClient false; hosted-host player=isServer false/isClient TRUE; remote client=isServer false/isClient true; dedicated/coop-server=isServer true/isClient false. The reliable discriminator for 'is the authoritative server logic in MY process' is `not isClient()` (true for SP, dedicated, and the hosted coop-server). Canonical fix: in requestSync, if not isClient() then call MasteryManager:buildSyncPayload(player) (or equivalent) directly + apply to the local cache + clear the awaiting flag synchronously; else send the command and wait. One codebase serves SP + hosted + dedicated. This is the canonical dedicated->SP-compat conversion pattern.

truths.summary: RESOLVED 2026-05-31: the correct API is Perks.FromString(key), a method on the Perks global (registered implicitly by the engine at runtime). The bare top-level global PerksFromString does NOT exist in B42.18 and never has - vanilla Lua uses Perks.FromString consistently. Workshop mod 3666281346 calls bare PerksFromString and therefore has a latent nil-reference bug that fires when its code path executes.
truths.details:
Resolution path:
1. Gemini investigation (docs/tracking/PERKSFROMSTRING_LOCATION_2026-05-31.md): grep of the live B42.18 install (media/lua/ and the zombie/ jar classes) returned ZERO hits for `PerksFromString`, but MULTIPLE hits for `Perks.FromString` in vanilla Lua: media/lua/server/Foraging/forageSystem.lua, media/lua/server/Vehicles/Vehicles.lua, media/lua/client/ISUI/ISInventoryPaneContextMenu.lua, and others. Perks.FromString is established (though undocumented) vanilla usage.
2. Runtime probes (SP + hosted-host + embedded coop server, 2026-05-31): api.PerksFromString=absent in every env at shared-load. Confirms the negative claim independently of the source grep.
3. Source binding: Perks.FromString is registered dynamically/implicitly by the engine (Gemini did not find a static declaration in shared Lua or in _exposed_classes.txt's PerkFactory binding). Probably set up as an entry on a Perks table at LuaManager init time. Mechanism not verified, but the function's existence and call signature are.

Correct usage:
  local perk = Perks.FromString('Maintenance')
  if perk then character:LevelPerk(perk) end

Incorrect (will nil-ref):
  local perk = PerksFromString('Maintenance')   -- bare global, does not exist

Supersedes (both DEPRECATED 2026-05-31):
  - perks-from-string-global

truths.summary: In B42 MP a player's BodyDamage/health is SERVER-authoritative. Body-damage writes (setHealth, bodyPart:setHealth, generateDeepWound, setBleedingTime, setOverallBodyHealth) applied from a CLIENT / local-player context are reverted by the server within a tick (the 'wound heals over and over' symptom). The SAME writes applied SERVER-SIDE on the player's IsoPlayer persist, sync down to the client with no transmit, and kill via the engine's own health sim. To injure or kill a player reliably in MP, do body-damage SERVER-SIDE.

truths.summary: IsoGameCharacter death entry points differ in networking. truths.summary: CharacterTrait.register() IDs must be fully lowercase to match the script system's ResourceLocation lookups, or a silent orphaned handle is created.
truths.details: The script parser resolves the CharacterTrait field in character_trait_definition blocks via CharacterTrait.get(ResourceLocation.of(id)). ResourceLocation normalises the namespace to lowercase but preserves path capitalisation. If registries.lua registers with a mixed-case path (e.g. "BBCommonSenseMedical:MedicalPractitioner"), the registry entry key is "bbcommonsensemedical:MedicalPractitioner". The script block uses a lowercase path ("bbcommonsensemedical:medicalpractitioner"), which does not match. Two separate CharacterTrait objects are created. Profession GrantedTraits lookups, hasTrait() calls, and chargen all use the script-system handle (lowercase). The registries.lua handle is an orphan — never found, causing silently missed profession grants and false hasTrait() returns with no error. Fix: all IDs passed to CharacterTrait.register() must be fully lowercase namespaced IDs matching the script block CharacterTrait field exactly.

truths.summary: sandbox-options.txt parser is strict: one malformed option silently rejects the entire file and the mod's sandbox page vanishes with no log entry.
truths.details:
Every option block must end with `translation = ...,` (trailing comma required). The file header must be `VERSION = 1,`. A single syntax error anywhere — including an unsupported type value or missing trailing comma — causes the PZ parser to discard the whole file silently.

The `SandboxVars.<ModId>` table is nil until the first save loads with the mod active — always nil-guard before accessing it:
```lua
local sv = SandboxVars and SandboxVars.MyMod
if not sv then return end
```

Debug strategy: remove options one by one to isolate the bad block, since there are no parse error messages.

truths.summary: To add GrantedTraits to a vanilla profession, declare a character_profession_definition block with the same ID in a mod script file — it replaces the vanilla entry via map.put() semantics.
truths.details: CharacterProfessionDefinitionScript stores definitions in a Java Map keyed by CharacterProfession handle. A second character_profession_definition block with the same fully-qualified ID (e.g. base:doctor) overwrites the previous entry. A mod can therefore extend a vanilla profession by reproducing all vanilla fields verbatim and appending new GrantedTraits. Multiple granted traits are separated by semicolons: GrantedTraits = base:nightowl;bbcommonsensemedical:medicalpractitioner. The overriding mod's script file must be placed in media/scripts/characters/ and can use any module name since fully-qualified IDs resolve independently of module context. Maintenance risk: if the vanilla profession definition changes (new XPBoosts, GrantedRecipes) the mod's copy must be updated. Only override the minimum set of professions needed. All trait IDs in GrantedTraits must be fully lowercase (see b42.registry.charactertrait.lowercase-required) or the grant silently fails at script-parse time. CONFLICT NOTE: two mods overriding the same profession = last loader wins silently; load-order matters.

truths.summary: Since B42.13, ISBaseTimedAction subclasses MUST be declared as globals (not local variables) or they break in multiplayer.
truths.details:
In B41 it was acceptable to declare `local MyAction = ISBaseTimedAction:derive('MyAction')`. In B42.13+ local variables go out of scope during MP synchronization causing subtle failures — actions may not complete or may cause desync.

The class MUST be assigned to the global namespace with a mod-prefixed name:
```lua
MyMod_MyAction = ISBaseTimedAction:derive('MyMod_MyAction')  -- CORRECT
-- NOT: local MyMod_MyAction = ...
```
This applies to any file under media/lua/client/ that defines a timed action.

truths.summary: In timed actions, store item:getID() in the constructor — not the item reference — because object refs go stale in MP; re-resolve from inventory in perform().
truths.details:
InventoryItem object references captured at queue time can become stale during multiplayer synchronization by the time perform() fires.

Safe pattern:
```lua
function MyMod_MyAction.new(character, item)
    local o = ISBaseTimedAction.new(character)
    o.targetItemId = item:getID()  -- store ID, not item ref
    return o
end

function MyMod_MyAction:perform()
    local inv = self.character:getInventory()
    local item = inv:getItemById(self.targetItemId)  -- re-resolve
    if not item then
        ISBaseTimedAction.perform(self)
        return
    end
    -- use item safely
    ISBaseTimedAction.perform(self)
end

function MyMod_MyAction:isValid()
    local inv = self.character:getInventory()
    return inv:containsID(self.targetItemId)  -- check by ID
end
```

truths.summary: ISTimedActionQueue provides add(action) and clear(character). For queue inspection, use hasActionType(character, type) and getTimedActionQueue(character).current / .queue[1]. The methods addFront/isQueued/getAction documented in older B41 guides DO NOT EXIST in B42.18 vanilla.
truths.details:
Confirmed methods (B42.18 vanilla `media/lua/client/TimedActions/ISTimedActionQueue.lua`):
- `ISTimedActionQueue.add(action)` — appends to queue (line 134)
- `ISTimedActionQueue.clear(character)` — cancels all queued actions for a character (line 183)
- `ISTimedActionQueue.hasActionType(character, type)` — checks by class-name string (line 203)
- `ISTimedActionQueue.getTimedActionQueue(character)` — returns the queue object; access `.current` for the running action or `.queue[1]` for the next queued one

```lua
-- Check if action is already queued before adding:
if not ISTimedActionQueue.hasActionType(player, 'MyMod_MyAction') then
    ISTimedActionQueue.add(MyMod_MyAction:new(player, item))
end

-- Inspect currently-running action:
local q = ISTimedActionQueue.getTimedActionQueue(player)
local running = q and q.current  -- nil if no action active
local next_q = q and q.queue and q.queue[1]
```

DO NOT use: `addFront`, `isQueued`, `getAction` — these are documented in older B41 guides but DO NOT EXIST in B42.18 vanilla ISTimedActionQueue. Verified absent via `media/lua` grep 2026-05-31.

truths.summary: Both perform() AND stop() MUST call their ISBaseTimedAction super method or the action queue gets stuck / animation freezes.
truths.details:
Two mandatory super calls in custom timed actions:

1. `ISBaseTimedAction.perform(self)` MUST be the last line of perform() — omitting it leaves the action queue stuck, no further actions will run.

2. `ISBaseTimedAction.stop(self)` MUST be called in stop() — omitting it leaves the character animation frozen.

Both are non-optional even in early-return paths:
```lua
function MyMod_MyAction:perform()
    -- early return case still needs super:
    if someCondition then
        ISBaseTimedAction.perform(self)  -- still required
        return
    end
    -- normal logic
    ISBaseTimedAction.perform(self)  -- last line
end

function MyMod_MyAction:stop()
    ISBaseTimedAction.stop(self)  -- required or animation freezes
end
```

truths.summary: getText(key) returns the key string on a miss (never nil), so every player-facing string must go through a per-mod tr(key, fallback, ...) helper that treats `result == key` as a miss and returns the fallback, with %N varargs substitution; bare getText() silently shows raw translation keys to players.

BB Common Sense Core implements this well and is the exemplar; CSR_Fundamentals has no suite-level tr() and uses bare getText in several context menus (the anti-pattern). truths.summary: A mod tested only on a dedicated server can ship client-path crashes that NEVER surface in dedicated boot logs, because client-side event handlers (OnGameStart client code, panel open, HUD callbacks) don't execute in the dedicated server process. These crashes only appear in SP / hosted-host runs. Corollary: mod_audit on a dedicated boot alone is INSUFFICIENT to certify a mod functional — an SP boot is required to exercise client paths.
truths.details: Surfaced 2026-06-01 by MasterySystem SP test. MasteryManager.lua:612 calls applyAttrTierBonuses() which is a local function defined at line 676 (after the call site, inside an earlier-defined function initAttrPointsRetroactive at 592). Classic Lua forward-reference: the local is nil as an upvalue at call time -> 'Object tried to call nil' crash. This crash fires on the client path (openPanel -> requestSync -> initAttrPointsRetroactive, and onGameStart -> requestSync), which NEVER runs on a dedicated server -- so 4.7's dedicated-boot mod_audit reported 0 mod-attributed errors while the mod was in fact completely UI-broken in SP. The mod was authored for dedicated/client deployment; the SP code path was never exercised pre-2026-06-01. Audit-process implication: certify mods via BOTH a dedicated boot AND an SP boot before declaring functional. Fix for the forward-reference class: forward-declare the local before the first referencing function, or reorder definitions.

truths.details: Surfaced 2026-06-01 by MasterySystem SP test (Grok diagnosis). Fix: anchor to the hovered node's post-scroll screen coords (or mouse + live scroll comp) AND clamp tx/ty into the panel's getAbsoluteX/Y + width/height rect. truths.summary: A full-screen ISUIElement added via addToUIManager() blocks all mouse events even if Lua isMouseOver() returns false — Java does bounds check first.
truths.details:
B42's Java UIManager performs its own bounding-box test before calling any Lua method on the element. A full-screen element (0,0,screenW,screenH) always passes the Java bounds check regardless of what Lua isMouseOver() returns. Overriding isMouseOver, onMouseDown, onMouseUp etc. has no effect.

Fix: do NOT call addToUIManager() on draw-only overlays. Instead render via Events.OnPostUIDraw:
```lua
Events.OnPostUIDraw.Add(function()
    local o = ensureOverlay()
    if not o then return end
    o:render()
end)
```

truths.summary: ISPanel:render() fires BEFORE children in B42's render pipeline — do NOT draw tooltips or overlays inline inside render().
truths.details: PZ B42 UI pipeline order for any ISPanel: prerender() → render() → [each child: prerender → render → children]. This means anything drawn via self:drawRect/drawText inside render() appears UNDERNEATH all child ISPanels. If you draw a tooltip box in render(), every child node box renders on top of it and the tooltip is invisible. Fix: add the tooltip as a separate ISPanel via addToUIManager() — UIManager-level panels render after all game panels and are always on top.

truths.summary: Never call view:createChildren() before ISTabPanel:addView(name, view). The framework calls createChildren() automatically via instantiate() when addChild() is invoked inside addView. Calling it early causes premature javaObject creation outside the parent Java hierarchy, making the tab click-inert.
truths.details:
B42 PZ UI lifecycle (ISUIElement.lua):
1. ISUIElement:instantiate() creates the javaObject AND immediately calls self:createChildren().
2. ISUIElement:addChild(child) calls child:instantiate() if child.javaObject == nil — this is the correct moment to create the javaObject inside the parent's AddChild call.
3. ISTabPanel:addView(name, view) calls self:addChild(view), which triggers instantiate() → createChildren() in the right order.

If createChildren() is called BEFORE addView():
- The first self:addChild(child) inside rebuild() finds self.javaObject == nil, triggering self:instantiate()
- instantiate() creates the javaObject THEN calls createChildren() recursively → double rebuild with duplicate children
- javaObject is now created outside the parent's AddChild call
- When addView() later calls addChild(view), javaObject != nil so instantiate() is SKIPPED
- The panel is added via AddChild directly, bypassing the instantiate() registration that PZ's Java event dispatch requires
- Result: tab renders and hover-highlights correctly (draw loop walks child tree) but click events are not dispatched (event registration was missed)

Vanilla pattern (ISCharacterInfoWindow.lua:127-149): every view is `view:new(...) → view:initialise() → panel:addView(name, view)` — NO explicit createChildren() before addView.

Fix: remove any explicit createChildren() call between initialise() and addView().
evidence: MasterySystem MASTFIX3: ISCharacterInfoWindow_MasteryTab.lua line 52 removed — was `self.masteryView:createChildren()` between initialise() and addView(); removing it fixed the click-inert Mastery tab
ISUIElement.lua:846-860 (B42 vanilla): instantiate() creates javaObject then calls self:createChildren() — framework-controlled single call
ISUIElement.lua:1232-1233 (B42 vanilla): addChild() calls otherElement:instantiate() only if otherElement.javaObject == nil — skipped if javaObject already created
ISCharacterInfoWindow.lua:127-149 (B42 vanilla): all 5 vanilla tabs use new() → initialise() → addView() with NO createChildren() before addView — the correct pattern

observations: MasterySystem SP probe 2026-06-05: Mastery tab functional in Character Info window — no click-inert behaviour, zero Mastery UI errors; ISCharacterInfoWindow_MasteryTab.lua uses new()->initialise()->addView() pattern without pre-calling createChildren()

truths.summary: ISPanel:onMouseMove(dx, dy) passes DELTA movement, not current screen-absolute position — use getMouseX()/getMouseY() for the current cursor location.
truths.details: A common trap: override onMouseMove expecting absolute mouse coords and subtract getAbsoluteX()/Y() to get panel-local position. In B42, onMouseMove receives (dx, dy) — the movement delta since last frame. Subtracting absolute panel position from a delta gives wildly wrong values. Correct pattern: use getMouseX()/getMouseY() (always screen-absolute) and subtract self:getAbsoluteX()/self:getAbsoluteY() to get panel-local coords.

Replaced with getMouseX()/getMouseY() poll — matches behavior of update() which uses the same approach and works reliably

truths.summary: Floating ISPanel tooltips must addToUIManager on each show and removeFromUIManager on each hide — plus setAlwaysOnTop(true) — to stay above the render stack
truths.details:
PZ's UIManager render stack is insertion-ordered. Calling addToUIManager() once at panel-creation time permanently places the tooltip behind every UI element that opens afterwards. There is no automatic Z-promotion.

The correct pattern (matches ISToolTip and sandbox options label mods):

```lua
-- At creation: flag only, NO addToUIManager
tt:setAlwaysOnTop(true)
_tooltipPanel = tt   -- don't call tt:addToUIManager() here

-- showTooltip:
if not _tooltipPanel:getIsVisible() then
    _tooltipPanel:addToUIManager()   -- re-inserts at TOP of render stack
    _tooltipPanel:setVisible(true)
end

-- hideTooltip:
if _tooltipPanel and _tooltipPanel:getIsVisible() then
    _tooltipPanel:setVisible(false)
    _tooltipPanel:removeFromUIManager()
end
```

The getIsVisible() guards prevent double-add and double-remove. setAlwaysOnTop(true) is a secondary safety flag — re-adding on each show is the primary mechanism. Both are needed.

Reference: ISLabelMod (ssr_core, Workshop 1178769629) uses identical pattern for ISToolTip.
evidence: ISMasteryPanel tooltips were rendering at the bottom of the screen behind the main panel — root cause was single addToUIManager call in createChildren()/ensureTooltip(), placing tooltip permanently below all panels opened after it

Fixed by removing addToUIManager from ensureTooltip(), adding setAlwaysOnTop(true), and switching to per-show add / per-hide remove pattern — tooltips now appear correctly above all UI at cursor position
ISLabelMod (mod 1178769629) confirmed pattern: addToUIManager in updateTooltip when not visible, removeFromUIManager when mouseOver false

truths.summary: IsoUtils.XToScreen in B42 returns a merged (x,y) incorporating camera offsets — do not subtract IsoCamera.getOffX/Y manually
truths.details: In Build 41, world-to-screen projection required manual camera offset subtraction. In Build 42, IsoUtils.XToScreen(x, y, z, 0) already incorporates the camera offset and returns the final screen coordinates directly as two return values (sx, sy). If you additionally subtract IsoCamera.getOffX() or use the deprecated YToScreen, the result is offset by thousands of pixels or fails to render entirely. Correct pattern: `local sx, sy = IsoUtils.XToScreen(x, y, z, 0)` — use these values directly for UI/FX positioning without any further camera adjustment.

truths.summary: Calling vehicle:toggleLockedDoor() directly on the client has no effect in dedicated-server MP — door state changes must be sent to the server via sendClientCommand.
truths.details:
Only the server owns vehicle door state in dedicated MP. The correct pattern:
1. Client sends stable vehicle and part IDs (never indices, which can shift) via sendClientCommand
2. Server re-validates and calls vehicle:toggleLockedDoor(part, player, false)
3. Server calls vehicle:transmitPartDoor(part) to sync to all clients

Critical: do NOT re-check door:isLocked() in isValid() of a timed action — lock state changes in perform() server-side, so re-checking in isValid() will cancel the client action prematurely.

```lua
-- Client side:
local args = { vehicleId = veh:getID(), partId = part:getId() }
sendClientCommand(player, 'MyMod', 'toggleDoor', args)

-- Server side:
Events.OnClientCommand.Add(function(module, cmd, player, args)
    if module ~= 'MyMod' or cmd ~= 'toggleDoor' then return end
    local veh = getVehicleById(args.vehicleId)
    local part = veh and veh:getPartById(args.partId)
    if not part then return end
    veh:toggleLockedDoor(part, player, false)
    veh:transmitPartDoor(part)
end)
```
evidence: api-quick-reference.md — Vehicle Door Lock/Unlock (B42 MP Pattern) section

truths.summary: Wrapping ISEquipWeaponAction:complete() to re-equip an off-hand item creates a feedback loop that prevents primary-hand pistol equipping.
truths.details:
Vanilla has reciprocal handgun-slot logic: equipping a pistol may clear the secondary slot. If complete() is wrapped to immediately re-equip the off-hand pistol, it triggers an infinite loop.

Fix: wrap ISEquipWeaponAction.perform instead, add early-exit when a handgun is already in primary hand, and use Events.OnPlayerAttackFinished for post-attack off-hand restoration. Do NOT wrap complete():

```lua
-- WRONG: creates feedback loop
local origComplete = ISEquipWeaponAction.complete
ISEquipWeaponAction.complete = function(self)
    origComplete(self)
    reEquipOffHand()  -- triggers another equip, loops
end

-- CORRECT: hook perform instead
local origPerform = ISEquipWeaponAction.perform
ISEquipWeaponAction.perform = function(self)
    local primary = self.character:getPrimaryHandItem()
    if primary and primary:isAimedFirearm() then return end  -- early exit
    origPerform(self)
end
Events.OnPlayerAttackFinished.Add(restoreOffHand)
```
evidence: B42_known_problem_patterns.md — Pattern 17: ISEquipWeaponAction:complete() Wrapper Creates Feedback Loop

truths.summary: Standardized mod dev workflow: _workspace (edit) -> _staging (gate pass) -> _probe (test) -> Contents/mods (publish)
truths.details:
Standardized mod development folder structure under Workshop root:

```
<WorkshopRoot>/
├── _workspace/           # ACTIVE DEVELOPMENT (edit here)
│   ├── <ModName>/        # Full mod layout (Contents/mods/<ModId>/42/...)
│   └── ...
├── _staging/             # READY FOR PROBE TESTING (copied from _workspace after gate PASS/REVIEW)
│   └── <ModName>/
├── _probe/               # PROBE BOOT TARGET (modlist.txt + symlinks or copies from _staging)
│   └── modlist.txt       # List of mod folder names to enable for pz-sp/mp-probe
├── Contents/mods/        # WORKSHOP PUBLISHED (clean, validated, final)
│   └── <ModId>/          # Steam upload format
└── test server/          # DEPRECATED — remove after migration
```

**Flow:**
1. Edit in `_workspace/<Mod>/`
2. Run static audits (`space_production_release_gate`) on `_workspace/<Mod>`
3. Copy to `_staging/<Mod>/` when gate passes (REVIEW/PASS)
4. Update `_probe/modlist.txt` with mods from `_staging/`
5. Run probe (`pz-sp-probe` / `pz-mp-probe`) pointing at `_probe/`
6. Analyze `console.txt` with `space_analyze_pz_log` → `sp`/`mp` evidence for truths
7. After probe clean → copy `_staging/<Mod>/` to `Contents/mods/<ModId>/` for Workshop upload

**Rules:**
- `_workspace/`, `_staging/`, `_probe/` are local-only (gitignored, not uploaded)
- PZ only loads from `Contents/mods/` and Steam workshop — dev folders are invisible
- Underscore prefix is existing convention (`_archive`, `_staging`, `_temp`, `_patches`)
- Each mod in `_workspace/` maintains full Workshop layout (workshop.txt, preview.png, Contents/mods/<ModId>/42/...)
- `_probe/modlist.txt` contains folder names matching `_staging/` entries

truths.summary: Workshop upload fails with 'error code 2' when workshop.txt id= references a Steam Workshop item ID that does not exist or is not owned by the uploader. Fix: set id= to the correct owned item ID, or 0 (empty) for a brand-new submission.
truths.details: Steam's Workshop API returns error code 2 (EResult::kEResultInvalidParam or item-not-found) when the item ID supplied to the upload call does not resolve to a Workshop item owned by the authenticated account. In PZ B42 Workshop uploads the item ID comes from the id= field in workshop.txt. A stale, mis-copied, or placeholder ID that belongs to a different item or no item causes an immediate upload failure with no further diagnostic. The fix is to audit workshop.txt and ensure id= matches the real Steam Workshop item ID for that mod under the uploader's account. For a first-time submission that has no Workshop item yet, id= must be 0 or omitted so PZ/Steam creates a new item. Evidence: Hubber/workshop.txt contained id=3729470883 which resolves to no Steam item owned by the uploader; changing to the real Hubber item id=3724452972 produced a successful upload. This is a pure tooling/workflow trap — it has no runtime Lua component and does not require an SP or MP boot to verify; a successful Steam upload is the definitive proof.
evidence: Owner-verified 2026-06-05: Hubber/workshop.txt id=3729470883 (non-existent/unowned item) -> Workshop upload error code 2
Owner-verified 2026-06-05: Hubber/workshop.txt id=3724452972 (correct Hubber Workshop item, owner-authenticated) -> upload SUCCEEDED
No Lua runtime component; Steam API error code 2 is the sole observable failure signal
enforced_by: workshop.txt id= field must match an owned Steam Workshop item ID
Use id=0 or omit id= for brand-new Workshop submissions

truths.summary: World-placed item FBX files (WorldStaticModel) must go in media/models_X/, not media/models/, or the item renders invisible with no log error.
truths.details:
PZ B42 uses two separate model directories:
- `media/models/` — character/player/zombie animation meshes
- `media/models_X/` — world-placed static item models referenced via WorldStaticModel in script blocks

Placing an FBX in media/models/ when it is referenced as a WorldStaticModel silently produces an invisible world object with no error in the log.

Script example: `mesh = MadnessAndMayhem/scppose1` resolves to `models_X/MadnessAndMayhem/scppose1.fbx`.

When building the script block, use:
```
WorldStaticModel
{
    mesh = MyMod/myItem,
    ...
}
```
and place the FBX at `media/models_X/MyMod/myItem.fbx`.

FileSystem: media/models/ contains only non-static animation text definitions (e.g., kate.txt, Vehicles_Ambulance.txt).
Script analysis: models_items.txt definitions (e.g., BlowTorch, Hoodie_Ground) use 'mesh = ...' paths that align with assets found in media/models_X/WorldItems/ and media/models_X/Static/.
This confirms media/models_X/ is the canonical location for static world models referenced by WorldStaticModel scripts.

truths.summary: If a world save references a dictionary string from a mod that is no longer loaded, the SERVER still boots fine but every JOINING CLIENT fails world-load with WorldDictionaryException 'Missing dictionary string on client: <string>'. Fix: fresh world, or restore the mod that registers the string.
truths.details: World saves bake registered dictionary strings (item types, UI layout strings, etc.) into the WorldDictionary. If the registering mod is later removed from the server's mod set (or its source vanishes — e.g. local mods dir wiped, workshop item missing), the server tolerates the stale reference at boot, but clients crash during GameLoadingState at StringDictionary$StringRegister.parseLoadListClient with 'Missing dictionary string on client: <X>' followed by 'Cannot load world due to WorldDictionary error'. Diagnosis: identify the owning mod from the string prefix (e.g. NC_HandCraftPanelLayout -> Neat_Crafting), then check whether the server still has ANY source for that mod (workshop content + local mods dir). Remedies: (a) fresh world (wipe-world:save) — right for disposable/staging worlds; (b) restore the registering mod (add its workshop ID back to WorkshopItems= and keep it in Mods=) — right when the world data must survive. Note the asymmetry: server-side load tolerates it, so the breakage only appears when a client tries to join.
evidence: runtime_client_to_dedicated: 2026-06-10 — owner's client failed to join pz-test (B42.19.0) with 'Missing dictionary string on client: NC_HandCraftPanelLayout' at StringDictionary.parseLoadListClient + 'Cannot load world due to WorldDictionary error'. Server-side verification: pz-test was STARTED and healthy; its Mods= listed Neat_Crafting but NO workshop item in its content tree provided the mod and its local mods dir was empty — the world predated the mod's removal. Client console showed zero Neat_Crafting load lines (mod never loaded client-side).
Prior owner experience recorded in CLAUDE.md Common Gotchas: 'WorldDictionary stale entries from removed mods block client world-load → fresh world fixes it.'
enforced_by: pre-wipe modlist validation: every Mods= entry must have a loadable source before world creation

truths.summary: B42 engine resets zombie walkType and animation variables every frame — throttled re-assertion causes flickering; reassert in OnZombieUpdate every frame
truths.details: The Build 42 animation engine re-evaluates and resets zombie:setWalkType() and zombie:setVariable() values every frame as part of its animation state machine. If you assert a custom walkType or animation variable on a throttled timer (e.g. once every 10 frames, or in EveryOneMinute), the engine overwrites it in the intervening frames and the animation flickers or never plays at all. Correct pattern: register a persistent OnZombieUpdate hook and call zombie:setWalkType() and zombie:setVariable() on every frame tick for as long as the custom state is active. Remove the hook (or stop asserting) only when you want the animation to revert to default.
evidence: Mod 3738217328 — zombie:setWalkType() and setVariable() re-asserted every OnZombieUpdate frame for custom boss animation states
owner-verified: owner extracted and confirmed this trap from direct analysis of mod 3738217328

truths.summary: Throttled loops cause moodle flickering in aura effects — pin stats every frame via OnPlayerUpdate to prevent decay between ticks
truths.details: When applying aura effects (panic, stress, sickness) to players near a special zombie, using EveryOneMinute or a thinned OnZombieUpdate counter causes visible moodle flickering: the stat decays between ticks, producing a pulsing effect as the player enters/leaves the effect radius. The correct pattern is to hook OnPlayerUpdate and force-set the stat to the 'demand' level every frame while the player is in range. Implementation: (1) maintain a maxDemand variable per player tracking the highest panic/stress requested by all nearby zombies, (2) in OnPlayerUpdate, call player:getStats():setPanic(maxDemand) (or equivalent) every frame. The stat is 'pinned' and cannot decay until the player physically leaves the aura radius and the demand is cleared to 0. Only clear the demand when no qualifying zombies remain within range.
evidence: Mod 3738217328 — aura stat pinning implementation using OnPlayerUpdate maxDemand pattern, eliminating flickering from throttled update loops
owner-verified: owner extracted and confirmed this pattern from direct analysis of mod 3738217328

truths.summary: When using IsoZombie as an NPC body (banditizing), must set zombie:setVariable('ZombieHitReaction', 'Chainsaw') or human-combat states cause a black screen.
truths.details:
When placing a zombie into human-combat states for NPC behavior, zombie:setVariable('ZombieHitReaction', 'Chainsaw') MUST be set. Without it, the engine's testDefense() dereferences moodles the zombie lacks and the screen goes black.

Also: setWalkType, setBumpType, and setAnimatingBackwards must be re-asserted every AI tick as the engine reverts them each frame.

```lua
local function initNPC(zombie)
    zombie:setVariable('ZombieHitReaction', 'Chainsaw')  -- required
    zombie:setWalkType('Normal')
    zombie:setBumpType('Shove')
    zombie:setAnimatingBackwards(false)
end

-- Re-assert every tick because engine reverts:
local function onZombieUpdate(zombie)
    if not zombie.myMod_isNPC then return end
    zombie:setWalkType('Normal')  -- re-assert each frame
end
```
evidence: B42_Globals_API.md — NPC / Zombie spawning section: ZombieHitReaction crash guard

truths.summary: dressInNamedOutfit at runtime does not persist to corpse — spawn-replace with addZombiesInOutfit to bake a persistent outfit
truths.details: Calling zombie:dressInNamedOutfit() at runtime dresses the live zombie visually, but the outfit ID is not baked into the zombie's permanent record. On death or chunk reload the zombie reverts to its original spawn outfit, causing visual inconsistency on the corpse. To guarantee a persistent custom outfit: (1) decide the mutation/outfit type at spawn time, (2) immediately remove the vanilla zombie from the world, (3) use addZombiesInOutfit with the target outfit name to spawn a new zombie at the same tile. The persistentOutfitId is baked at the moment of addZombiesInOutfit, ensuring the corpse retains the correct appearance after death and across chunk reloads.
evidence: Mod 3738217328 — spawn-replace pattern used to bake outfit IDs and ensure corpse visual integrity after OnZombieDead

truths.summary: zombie:getPersistentOutfitID() returns a Java Long, not a Lua number; mask off bit 16 for a stable per-zombie primary key.
truths.details:
getPersistentOutfitID() gives a stable per-zombie primary key that survives save/load and headwear toggling (with bit 16, the 'hat' bit, masked off). Use instead of getID()/getOnlineID() for persistent per-NPC data.

Critical: the return value is a Java Long, NOT a Lua number. Do not use it in Lua arithmetic directly. Use Long.parseUnsignedLong bit helpers or convert to string for map keys:

```lua
-- Use as string key (safe):
local key = tostring(zombie:getPersistentOutfitID())
npcData[key] = { health = 100 }

-- Do NOT do arithmetic directly:
-- local masked = outfitId & 0xFFFF  -- Java Long, not Lua number, will error
```
evidence: B42_Globals_API.md — NPC / Zombie spawning section: getPersistentOutfitID Java Long caveat

observations: B42_Globals_API.md zombie section: getPersistentOutfitID returns Java Long
Mask off bit 16 with band(0x7FFF) or similar for stable identity
Direct arithmetic on the raw return throws — must coerce/mask first

truths.summary: B42 MP wire-cap (~32.767) corrupts zombie HP over the network — use multi-phase respawn to create boss zombies above this limit
truths.details: Build 42 multiplayer has a wire-cap on zombie health of approximately 32.767 (likely an Int16 sign boundary). Any zombie with HP > 32.767 at the moment of network sync has its value corrupted and the zombie dies instantly on remote clients. To create 'boss' zombies with 100+ HP: (1) store the true budget in ModData (e.g. MZ_trueHP = 100), (2) clamp actual zombie health to 32.0 on spawn, (3) on OnZombieDead, if MZ_trueHP > 0, subtract the segment and immediately spawn a replacement at the same tile using addZombiesInOutfit with the same outfit. This creates a seamless multi-phase boss that never violates the wire-cap. The stored budget must survive across the respawn — attach it to the new zombie's ModData in the OnZombieDead handler.
evidence: Mod 3738217328 — working multi-phase boss implementation using MZ_trueHP ModData budget and addZombiesInOutfit respawn on OnZombieDead
owner-verified: owner extracted and confirmed this pattern from direct analysis of mod 3738217328

truths.summary: OnPlayerUpdate pattern: early returns for dead/asleep, SandboxVars config, AddWorldSound for AI sound, getWorldMarkers for visual. mod.info require= supports multiple deps via backslash. WARNING: hasTrait() is B42.19+ NPE.
truths.details:
Zombies-Hear-Your-Microphone (3004111200, updated Jun 2026) uses `OnPlayerUpdate` for per-frame logic:
```lua
function hotMic.onPlayerUpdate(playerObj)
    if playerObj:isDead() or playerObj:isAsleep() then return end
    -- microphone volume check, sound emission, visual markers
end
Events.OnPlayerUpdate.Add(hotMic.onPlayerUpdate)
```

**Key patterns**:
1. Early returns for dead/asleep players
2. `getCore():setTestingMicrophone(true)` enables microphone access
3. Uses `SandboxVars.ModName.option` for config
4. Checks `playerObj:isSneaking()`, `playerObj:isDead()`, `playerObj:isAsleep()
5. `AddWorldSound(playerObj, volume, radius)` for AI-audible sound
6. Visual markers via `getWorldMarkers()` only when option enabled

**Multiple mod dependencies**: mod.info uses backslash continuation:
```
require=\ChuckleberryFinnAlertSystem,\errorMagnifier
```
This declares multiple required mods (ChuckleberryFinnAlertSystem AND errorMagnifier). PZ loads both before this mod.

**CRITICAL**: Uses `playerObj:hasTrait(CharacterTrait.CONSPICUOUS)` which is **BROKEN in B42.19+** (NPE on missing trait). Should use Lua-side trait tracking per truth `b42.api.character_traits_remove_npe_guard`.

mod.info require= with backslash continuation for multiple deps

truths.summary: Events.AddXP fires AFTER XP is already committed — levels may have already bumped by handler time
truths.details: Events.AddXP.Add(function(player, perk, amount)) fires on both client (local player) and server (all players) after the XP has already been written to the player's XPSource. This means player:getPerkLevel(perk) may already reflect the new level inside the handler. To block vanilla XP gain you must call player:getXp():AddXP(perk, -amount) immediately. If the level already bumped, use player:setPerkLevel(perk, levelBefore) to force a rollback, then drain with -999999 in a loop to clear accumulated XP and prevent an immediate re-level.

truths.summary: Use `if not traits:get(handle)` to re-add a CharacterTrait after clearSkillTraits, not `hasTrait ~= nil and not hasTrait`. The nil-exclusive guard silently skips absent entries.
truths.details: getCharacterTraits():get(handle) returns nil when absent (after clearSkillTraits removes the entry) and false when present-but-inactive. Guard `hasTrait ~= nil and not hasTrait` only catches false, treating nil as already-active and skipping the add — traits are silently not re-applied after a clear+reapply cycle. Correct: `if not traits:get(handle) then traits:add(handle) end`. This matches the addVanillaTrait helper pattern already present in MasteryManager.lua. Fixed in MasteryManager.lua applySkillTraits() 2026-05-28.
evidence: MasteryManager.lua applySkillTraits() had three instances of the restrictive guard; all fixed 2026-05-28
addVanillaTrait() in same file already used the correct not-traits:get pattern
clearSkillTraits removes map entries entirely so subsequent get() returns nil not false

deprecation.reason: In-game B42.18 testing (2026-05-28) proved the pattern WRONG. `traits:get(handle)` itself NPEs at CharacterTraits.java:67 when called with a custom (runtime-registered via CharacterTrait.register) handle, because the player's CharacterTraits map is only pre-seeded with vanilla traits as inactive Boolean entries — custom handles are absent from the map, and Java's get() unboxes the null Boolean. The original bad pattern (hasTrait ~= nil and not hasTrait) was actually the LESS broken of the two because it short-circuited on the nil case. Pending agent research to find the actual safe pattern (likely TraitFactory-based or ModData-cached presence tracking) before promoting a replacement.

truths.summary: Derive mastery badge state (locked/started/available/complete) from cache + perk level using PROFESSION_LEVEL, CAPSTONE_LEVEL, MAX_EARLY_BONUSES, MAX_LATE_BONUSES.
truths.details: complete = spec+ult2 both set. available (pre-profession) = lvl >= PROFESSION_LEVEL OR lvl > earlyCount and earlyCount < MAX_EARLY_BONUSES. available (post-profession) = lvl >= CAPSTONE_LEVEL and lateCount >= MAX_LATE_BONUSES OR lvl > PROFESSION_LEVEL + lateCount and lateCount < MAX_LATE_BONUSES. started = has spec but nothing immediately available. locked = no mastery tree (check MasteryConfig.Data[skillName]) OR lvl < 1. Count earlyCount/lateCount by iterating bonusPicks keys: idx <= MAX_EARLY_BONUSES = early, else late. Never use MasteryConfig.ultimateSkillLevel or .baseSkillForRank1 — those fields do not exist.

truths.summary: MP clients must not write to player ModData — creates a local shadow that conflicts with server-transmitted data
truths.details: In multiplayer, player:getModData() on the client returns the locally cached copy. If client-side code writes to this table (e.g. md.MyMod = md.MyMod or {}), it creates entries that were never set by the server. When the server later calls transmitModData(), the client's local writes may be overwritten or cause merge confusion. Pattern: use two accessors — ensureDataWrite (creates/initialises the table, only called server-side or in SP) and ensureDataRead (returns a default table if the key is absent, never creates it). Gate with isMPClient() to choose which path to call.

truths.summary: On a ServerJockey host, NEVER run sudo/root file operations (backup/restore/move/copy) inside the runtime user's (sjgms) instance tree. Root-owned files break the PZ server on next boot: WorldDictionary.init() must write its backup into the active save dir, and if that dir is root-owned the runtime user (sjgms) gets Permission denied -> WorldDictionaryException -> 'Server Terminated' crash loop. Backups/restores must run AS the runtime user. The active save folder AND Server/<name>.ini must be sjgms-owned and name-matched.
truths.details: ServerJockey's PZ module selects the MOST-RECENTLY-MODIFIED Server/*.ini as the active config -- stray timestamped .bak-<ts>.ini files can hijack which world loads (PZ then launches under the backup world name). Keep Server/ to a single canonical <name>.ini. Recovery pattern: stop the instance, `sudo chown -R sjgms:nogroup` the save folder, `sudo mv` it back to the canonical name, `sudo rm` only the confirmed stray .bak-* inis (never the canonical .ini), then instance-scoped start. Blast-radius rule still applies: pz-temp instance only, never the SJ service unless the live instance is shut down first.
evidence: owner-verified 2026-06-05 incident: a prior root/sudo agent created servertest.bak-20260605-052137/ (root:root), deleted the original servertest/, and left a stray .bak .ini in Server/. ServerJockey selected the newest .ini (the .bak), PZ tried to write WorldDictionary/recorded_media into the root-owned save -> Permission denied -> crash loop. truths.summary: Use a global bypass flag to prevent recursive re-entry when manipulating XP inside Events.AddXP
truths.details: When calling player:getXp():AddXP() inside an Events.AddXP handler (to block or adjust XP), the call will fire Events.AddXP again recursively. Prevent infinite recursion with a global bypass flag: set _G.MOD_XP_BYPASS = true before the internal AddXP call, then clear it after. Check this flag at the top of your handler and return early if set. The flag must be _G scoped (not local) so it survives across the re-entrant call stack.

truths.summary: Guard server command handler files with a _G flag to prevent double-registration of OnClientCommand
truths.details: If a server-side Lua file that registers Events.OnClientCommand gets required more than once (via cross-require or hot-reload), the handler fires multiple times per command. Prevent this with a global flag at the top of the file: if _G.MyMod_Server_Handler then return end; _G.MyMod_Server_Handler = true. This is distinct from the env guard (isClient return) — the env guard prevents the file running on the wrong side; this guard prevents the handler being registered twice on the same side.
evidence: 3666281346 VanillaMenu_RPG_Server.lua lines 7-8: 'if _G.VM_RPG_Server_Handler then return end; _G.VM_RPG_Server_Handler = true'

RE-SCOPED 2026-05-31 (full-session FS2): required_evidence ['runtime_dedicated'] -> ['vanilla_source']. Rationale: Pattern truth - guard server command-handler files with a _G flag to prevent double-init of OnClientCommand. Mostly mod-author rule; vanilla doesn't double-register. Re-scope to vanilla_source.

observations: Pattern verification: While vanilla code typically manages event registration through modular loaders, the pattern of using a _G table or flag to protect idempotent registration of server command handlers (e.g., in mods like VM_RPG_Server) is a best-practice defense against hot-reload and cross-require issues.
This confirms the necessity and correctness of the guard pattern for mod developers, even if not explicitly required by vanilla script structures.

truths.summary: Use weak-key tables for any per-player state to prevent memory leaks when players disconnect
truths.details: When tracking per-player state (e.g. ignore flags, debug counters, cooldowns) in a module-level table keyed by the player object, use setmetatable({}, { __mode = 'k' }). This makes the keys weak references — when the IsoGameCharacter/IsoPlayer object is garbage collected after the player disconnects, the entry is automatically removed. Without this, player objects accumulate in memory for the session lifetime.
evidence: 3666281346 VM_RPG_XPIntercept_Server.lua lines 12-13: 'local IGNORE = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" })'
3666281346 VM_RPG_XPIntercept_Client.lua lines 11-12 — same pattern for DBG_COUNT

RE-SCOPED 2026-05-31 (full-session FS2): required_evidence ['runtime_dedicated'] -> ['vanilla_source']. Rationale: Pattern truth - weak-key tables for per-player state. Vanilla Lua doesn't broadly use this pattern. Re-scope to vanilla_source: evidence will be either Kahlua/Lua spec confirming weak-table support OR a successful mod-authored implementation.

observations: Language specification: Kahlua/Lua 5.1 supports weak tables via the '__mode' metatable field.
Pattern verification: The use of 'setmetatable(table, { __mode = "k" })' is the standard, idiomatically correct Lua pattern for preventing memory leaks in object-keyed tables.
This confirms the efficacy and validity of this pattern for per-player state tracking in B42 mods.

truths.summary: Production server fixes must follow pz-live read-only evidence -> pz-temp isolated clean-room proof -> pz-test live-equivalent validation -> explicitly approved pz-live push; never promote directly from pz-temp to pz-live.
truths.details:
Canonical production server-fix promotion workflow:

1. Use pz-live read-only evidence to establish the real symptom, baseline signatures, settings, and mod context.
2. Use pz-temp as a disposable isolated clean room. Reduce to the smallest useful mod/dependency/settings set, reproduce the issue, run probes, and A/B-test one candidate fix at a time to establish causality.
3. Use pz-test as the live-equivalent validation environment. The owner prepares it with the same settings and mods as pz-live; apply candidate fixes here and validate boot, joins, original reproduction, adjacent behavior, performance, and logs across the full stack.
4. Never promote directly from pz-temp to pz-live. A pz-temp pass proves isolated causality only; a pz-test pass proves compatibility with the live-equivalent stack.
5. After pz-test validation, package the exact delta, backup, rollback, and evidence. Any pz-live write or lifecycle action requires explicit owner approval for that exact push.
6. All ServerJockey actions must remain instance-scoped. Never operate the service/daemon itself, and never infer authorization for one instance from authorization for another.
